Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 25, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

Tabaraka alladhi nazzala al-Furqan… wa la nushura (Al-Furqan 25:1–3)

This opening makes clear what the central theme and subject of this surah is: that this Book is revealed from Allah, and that the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ) is for all of mankind. The basic message of this call is that Allah is One, without partner; He has no son and no associate; He alone is the Owner of this entire universe, He alone is the Manager, and He runs it with His wisdom and planning. Despite these realities, those who associate partners with Allah continue to associate partners; those who fabricate lies continue to fabricate; those who dispute continue to dispute; and those who transgress continue to cross their limits.

Tabaraka alladhi… nadhira (25:1): "Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion (al-Furqan) upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds." Tabaraka comes from barakah, in the form of the mufa'alah pattern, meaning "He is most blessed," that is, He is full of abundant bounties and blessings. Here, instead of naming Allah (Jalla Shanuhu) directly, the Being is referred to with the relative pronoun alladhi, "He who sent down the Furqan" (25:1). This is because the discussion in this surah concerns "truthfulness and prophethood," and the Divine Being has a deep connection with this, and also a connection with the revelation of the Quran, since it is that Being who sends it down.

The Quran is called al-Furqan here because the teachings it contains draw a very clear distinction between truth and falsehood, and between guidance and misguidance. Moreover, through it a clear distinction and difference is shown between the Islamic system of life and non-Islamic systems of life, and between the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah) and the Age of Islam. This is because Islam establishes in human consciousness and human conscience a clear way of life, and then practically establishes that way of life within human existence. In this manner, the Book and the Furqan have set this system apart and distinguished it from all the systems of the world. Thus the Quran is Furqan in the sense that it is a new era (ahd jadid) for humanity, separate and distinct from the old era, both in terms of concepts and ideas and in terms of practical life. The Quran is Furqan even in this broad sense. It is a point of divergence beyond which humanity has now reached maturity, and its age of childhood has ended. The period in which people were shown material miracles and had the difference between truth and falsehood explained to them has now ended. Now this difference will be explained through the judge of reason. Moreover, previously the scope of prophethood was limited and local, but now this prophethood has taken on a universal character. Liyakuna lil-'alamina nadhira (25:1): "that he may be a warner to all the worlds." In short, in all these meanings and spheres, this Book is the Furqan.

At the place of honour and exaltation of the Prophet (ﷺ), the word 'abd (servant) is used for him. The honour and exaltation of the Prophet (ﷺ) through the word 'abdihi ("His servant") was also shown at the occasion of the Isra and Mi'raj.

Subhana alladhi asra… ila al-masjid al-aqsa (17:1): "Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa." And in those surahs in which the Prophet (ﷺ) is shown standing before the Lord Most Generous in a state of supplication and communion, the word 'Abdullah is used for him as well; and just as here the word 'abdihi is used for him at the time of the descent of the Quran, so too it is used in Surah al-Kahf.

Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi anzala 'ala 'abdihi al-kitaba wa lam yaj'al lahu 'iwaja (18:1): "Praise be to Allah, who sent down the Book upon His servant and placed in it no crookedness." Using the word "servant" for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in these places is an elevation of his rank and a great honour to him. For a human being, the highest station is to become a servant of Allah. Therefore the word "servant" is used for him here. Beyond this is the station of divinity (uluhiyyah), which is specific to Allah alone. There is no partner with Allah, and no suspicion of sharing with Allah can arise, whether at the place of the descent of the Quran, or where a human being was taken up to the heavens, or where a mortal is at his high station of recognition and communion. It is precisely such stations that have become a source of confusion for some of the earlier prophets' devotees. It was on such stations that devotees slipped and fabricated fabulous beliefs that certain prophets were the son of God, or they adopted a conception of a relationship between servant and God other than the relationship of servitude and divinity. For this reason, whenever the station of honour and exaltation of the prophets comes up, the word "servant" is used for them in the Quran. The intention is to convey that this is the high and lofty station which any human being can attain.

Here it is stated that the purpose of sending down the Quran upon this chosen servant is liyakuna lil-'alamina nadhira (25:1): "that he may be a warner to all the worlds." These verses are Meccan. This shows that the Prophet (ﷺ) was appointed as a messenger for the whole world from the very beginning. As for the claim made by some orientalists that the Islamic call was initially a local call, but later, when it attained worldwide conquests, it took on the form of a global movement, their opinion was mistaken; this call was universal from the very beginning. If the teachings of the Quran are considered thoroughly, it becomes evident that their very temperament is universal. The methods and means that Islam adopted for spreading this call were all universal. And the very purpose of these teachings was to bring all of humanity out of one era and into another; to remove one system from within it and give it another system; and this work is to be done through this Book of Furqan, which Allah has sent down to warn the people of all the world of an evil end, and which He sent down upon His servant so that he might serve as a warner to all people. This call was indeed universal, but since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a resident of Makkah, his first confrontation had to be with the people of Makkah. Therefore it was the people of Makkah who rejected and opposed this call.

In short, blessed is He who sent down this Book upon His great servant, a Book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood and is a standard of truth.

Alladhi lahu mulku al-samawati… taqdira (25:2): "He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has taken no son, who has no partner in the dominion, who created everything and then determined it with due measure."

Here too, instead of using the Divine Name, the relative pronoun alladhi is used, meaning that the attributes being mentioned have a constant and continuous connection with Allah.

Alladhi lahu mulku al-samawati wa al-ard (25:2): "He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth." He has complete control over the heavens and the earth. They are in His possession. He fully disposes over them, and all changes within the heavens and the earth take place by His will and command.

Wa lam yattakhidh waladan (25:2): "He has not taken a son." Procreation is the natural law which Allah has established within His creation so that through it the continuity of "life" may be maintained. As for the Divine Being, since He is ever-enduring and everlasting, He has no need of the chain of procreation.

Wa lam yakun lahu shareekun fi al-mulk (25:2): "Nor has He any partner in the dominion." If one observes and analyzes the creation within the heavens and the earth, it will be found that its design was created by one single Creator. Within everything there is one law of power, and in all creation the working and the change are seen to belong to one single Being.

Wa khalaqa kulla shay'in faqaddarahu taqdira (25:2): "He created everything and then determined it with due measure." He determined its size and its form. He assigned it a task and a defined function. He determined its time and its place, and He harmonized it with the great existence of this universe.

Those scholars who have reflected upon the existence of this universe and the manner of its creation and composition, and every human being who ever reflects upon it, will be astonished. As the secrets hidden in the creation of the universe are unveiled, one becomes more and more certain that this universe did not come into existence by mere chance. Its composition is so fine and subtle that humans are incapable of even knowing its manifestations and effects, while we have so far observed only a small aspect of this universe. Yet as our discoveries advance, we find within this universe extremely wise governing laws. These laws are in harmony with this universe. The further our knowledge advances, the better we understand this verse.

Wa khalaqa kulla shay'in faqaddarahu taqdira (25:2): "He created everything and then determined it with a complete determination." Mr. A. Cressy Morrison, President of the New York Academy of Sciences, writes in his book "Man Does Not Stand Alone": "A person is overcome with astonishment when he reflects on the organization of this universe in its present form. It is an extremely wise arrangement. If the crust of the earth were a few steps thicker in proportion to its present size, plants and vegetation would have ceased to exist entirely."

"If the air were a little higher than its present position, the countless meteors that today burn up in the upper atmosphere would strike this terrestrial globe, because the speed of these meteors is 46 miles per second. Thus wherever they fell, they would burn whatever was capable of burning; and if their speed were reduced to the magnitude of a rifle bullet, they would all settle on the earth and stick, with terrible consequences. As for man, if even a small meteor passed near him whose speed is ninety times that of a rifle bullet, the heat of its mere passing would turn them into tiny dust."

"Allah has made this air to a specific density, and through this density pass those rays which have the effects on crops that they have, which kill germs and produce vitamins; but these rays do not harm man unless he remains in them beyond what is necessary. It is worth reflecting that poisonous gases are constantly emitted from the earth, yet the air, even under the continuous pollution of those gases, does not change the proportion that is necessary for human health. And it is these vast seas that maintain this balance, through which all kinds of life, food, moderate rain, habitation and vegetation receive life, and through which human life itself is sustained."

"At present oxygen in this air is 21 percent. If it were to increase to 50 percent, all material that is now capable of burning would catch fire entirely. A single spark would set the forests ablaze, and all the forests would explode in a flash. And if the oxygen in the air were to fall to 10 percent or lower, human life might, after centuries, adjust itself to this proportion, but human civilization would be deprived of many things it has today, for example fire and other energies."

"The regulation of these creatures and the natural balance within them is also extraordinary, so that no animal, however large its body and however clever it may be, is able to dominate this world."

"Indeed, man did this: by transferring plants and animals from one place to another, he tried to alter the balance that nature had established. And man received a severe punishment for this action, in that by disturbing this balance, animals, insects and plants had to face various diseases."

"The importance of this balance with respect to the existence of man can be well understood from the following incident. Some years ago in Australia a kind of thorny melon was cultivated. This cultivation was done as a protective hedge, but this crop spread so widely that within a short time it covered an area equal to England. It destroyed whole cities and the crops of the people were ruined, to the point that it became difficult for people to sow seed. People tried hard to control its spread, but it proved impossible. A danger arose for all of Australia that this thorny melon crop would take possession of it, and nothing was an obstacle to it."

"Entomologists spread throughout the world, began research, and eventually discovered an insect whose only food was this melon. This insect was also spreading at the same speed as the thorny melon. In Australia there was no natural obstacle to this insect either; it spread so widely that it reduced the thorny melon to nothing. As soon as the melon was destroyed, the insect too began to disappear. Only a very small quantity of it remained. It was as though nature had kept it in reserve against the spread of that melon. Thus did nature establish this arrangement to maintain order and balance."

"The question is: why did the malaria mosquito not dominate the whole world, such that our forefathers would have died from it, or that they would have acquired some means of protection against it? Similarly the same may be said of the yellow fever mosquito; in one season it advanced so far that it reached New York. Several kinds of mosquitoes are also found in the frozen sea. Likewise... the widespread extension of ... for what reasons did it not occur? It remained confined to its hot zones, and thus humanity was saved from the onslaught of its armies; otherwise human existence would have been wiped off the face of the earth. As for plague and other deadly epidemics and deadly germs, one may say that humanity itself had no medicines against these things until yesterday, so how did it survive? Moreover, until yesterday humanity was even ignorant of the basic principles of hygiene. So the survival of the human race in such circumstances is itself nothing short of a miracle."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 1–3 (part 2 of 2):

"Then consider that insects do not have lungs of the kind that human beings have. These insects breathe through certain tubes that are within their bodies. When these insects grow beyond a certain size, not enough oxygen can enter through those tubes to suffice for their bodies. For this reason, no insect grows larger than a few inches. Likewise, the wings of these insects are also not very long. Within the system of creation and formation of these creeping things, they cannot grow beyond a certain measure. Thus the system of qadr (divine measure) has restrained their spreading. In this way, this world has been saved from their onslaught. If this principle of proportion had not been placed for the insects, then human survival on this earth would not have been possible. Just think about natural man: if a red fly the size of a lion's body, or a spider the size of a lion's body, were to come against him, could man confront such things?"

"There are also other miracles in the physical and natural structure of animals, such that if these natural arrangements for animals did not exist, no animal, nor even any plant, would exist in this world."

Day after day, humans are encountering discoveries which show that Allah, the Exalted, has maintained an extremely precise and delicate balance within this creation, and that for all the creatures of the universe a fixed measure and weight has been established. As human knowledge advances, man begins to understand the meaning of this verse:

﴿And He created everything and determined it with precise measure﴾ (25:2). "But it is extremely regrettable that the polytheists are not grasping this truth."

﴿Yet they have taken, besides Him, deities that create nothing, while they are themselves created, and possess neither harm nor benefit for themselves, and possess neither death nor life nor resurrection﴾ (25:3). "People have, leaving Him, taken gods who create nothing, but are themselves created, who have no power to bring harm or benefit even to themselves, who can neither cause death, nor give life, nor raise the dead."

Thus Allah strips their self-made gods of all the attributes of divinity.

﴿They create nothing﴾ (25:3): while the Lord, the Exalted, has created all creation.

﴿And they are themselves created﴾ (25:3): that is, they were created by Allah Himself and brought into existence by Him. The Creator of all is Allah, whether they are angels, jinn, humans, trees, or stones.

﴿They have no power to bring harm or benefit even to themselves﴾ (25:3): To say nothing of harm or benefit to those who worship them. Sometimes it happens that someone has no power to bring benefit to himself but can cause harm; yet these deities are such that they have no power even to harm themselves. Therefore, the mention of harm is placed before benefit. That is, to inflict harm upon oneself is a very easy matter, yet these people cannot even manage that. After this, the attributes that belong exclusively to Allah are mentioned.

﴿They can neither cause death, nor give life, nor raise the dead﴾ (25:3): They can neither bring death to the living, nor create life, nor restore life to the dead. If they cannot do these things, then what kind of gods are they, and what is the basis on which the polytheists have made them gods?

This is clear misguidance. Following this, it is not strange that they say what they say against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, for when they speak such things about Allah, what they say about the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is not surprising. Can there be any act more abominable for a human being than to level accusations against Allah, when He is the Owner, the Creator, the Manager, and the Determiner of all things? The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was asked which sin is the most heinous, and he ﷺ said: "That you set up a rival to Allah while He is the One who created you." (Agreed upon) — *an taj'ala lillahi nidda wa huwa khalaqak*.

Having mentioned their audacity regarding the station of divinity, the passage now turns to their overstepping regarding the station of prophethood, and a critique is offered in response that clearly shows how small and baseless their objection is.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 25, verses 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

Tabaraka alladhi nazzala al-Furqan… wa la nushura (Al-Furqan 25:1–3)

This opening makes clear what the central theme and subject of this surah is: that this Book is revealed from Allah, and that the mission of Muhammad (ﷺ) is for all of mankind. The basic message of this call is that Allah is One, without partner; He has no son and no associate; He alone is the Owner of this entire universe, He alone is the Manager, and He runs it with His wisdom and planning. Despite these realities, those who associate partners with Allah continue to associate partners; those who fabricate lies continue to fabricate; those who dispute continue to dispute; and those who transgress continue to cross their limits.

Tabaraka alladhi… nadhira (25:1): "Blessed is He who sent down the Criterion (al-Furqan) upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds." Tabaraka comes from barakah, in the form of the mufa'alah pattern, meaning "He is most blessed," that is, He is full of abundant bounties and blessings. Here, instead of naming Allah (Jalla Shanuhu) directly, the Being is referred to with the relative pronoun alladhi, "He who sent down the Furqan" (25:1). This is because the discussion in this surah concerns "truthfulness and prophethood," and the Divine Being has a deep connection with this, and also a connection with the revelation of the Quran, since it is that Being who sends it down.

The Quran is called al-Furqan here because the teachings it contains draw a very clear distinction between truth and falsehood, and between guidance and misguidance. Moreover, through it a clear distinction and difference is shown between the Islamic system of life and non-Islamic systems of life, and between the Age of Ignorance (jahiliyyah) and the Age of Islam. This is because Islam establishes in human consciousness and human conscience a clear way of life, and then practically establishes that way of life within human existence. In this manner, the Book and the Furqan have set this system apart and distinguished it from all the systems of the world. Thus the Quran is Furqan in the sense that it is a new era (ahd jadid) for humanity, separate and distinct from the old era, both in terms of concepts and ideas and in terms of practical life. The Quran is Furqan even in this broad sense. It is a point of divergence beyond which humanity has now reached maturity, and its age of childhood has ended. The period in which people were shown material miracles and had the difference between truth and falsehood explained to them has now ended. Now this difference will be explained through the judge of reason. Moreover, previously the scope of prophethood was limited and local, but now this prophethood has taken on a universal character. Liyakuna lil-'alamina nadhira (25:1): "that he may be a warner to all the worlds." In short, in all these meanings and spheres, this Book is the Furqan.

At the place of honour and exaltation of the Prophet (ﷺ), the word 'abd (servant) is used for him. The honour and exaltation of the Prophet (ﷺ) through the word 'abdihi ("His servant") was also shown at the occasion of the Isra and Mi'raj.

Subhana alladhi asra… ila al-masjid al-aqsa (17:1): "Glory be to He who took His servant by night from al-Masjid al-Haram to al-Masjid al-Aqsa." And in those surahs in which the Prophet (ﷺ) is shown standing before the Lord Most Generous in a state of supplication and communion, the word 'Abdullah is used for him as well; and just as here the word 'abdihi is used for him at the time of the descent of the Quran, so too it is used in Surah al-Kahf.

Al-hamdu lillahi alladhi anzala 'ala 'abdihi al-kitaba wa lam yaj'al lahu 'iwaja (18:1): "Praise be to Allah, who sent down the Book upon His servant and placed in it no crookedness." Using the word "servant" for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in these places is an elevation of his rank and a great honour to him. For a human being, the highest station is to become a servant of Allah. Therefore the word "servant" is used for him here. Beyond this is the station of divinity (uluhiyyah), which is specific to Allah alone. There is no partner with Allah, and no suspicion of sharing with Allah can arise, whether at the place of the descent of the Quran, or where a human being was taken up to the heavens, or where a mortal is at his high station of recognition and communion. It is precisely such stations that have become a source of confusion for some of the earlier prophets' devotees. It was on such stations that devotees slipped and fabricated fabulous beliefs that certain prophets were the son of God, or they adopted a conception of a relationship between servant and God other than the relationship of servitude and divinity. For this reason, whenever the station of honour and exaltation of the prophets comes up, the word "servant" is used for them in the Quran. The intention is to convey that this is the high and lofty station which any human being can attain.

Here it is stated that the purpose of sending down the Quran upon this chosen servant is liyakuna lil-'alamina nadhira (25:1): "that he may be a warner to all the worlds." These verses are Meccan. This shows that the Prophet (ﷺ) was appointed as a messenger for the whole world from the very beginning. As for the claim made by some orientalists that the Islamic call was initially a local call, but later, when it attained worldwide conquests, it took on the form of a global movement, their opinion was mistaken; this call was universal from the very beginning. If the teachings of the Quran are considered thoroughly, it becomes evident that their very temperament is universal. The methods and means that Islam adopted for spreading this call were all universal. And the very purpose of these teachings was to bring all of humanity out of one era and into another; to remove one system from within it and give it another system; and this work is to be done through this Book of Furqan, which Allah has sent down to warn the people of all the world of an evil end, and which He sent down upon His servant so that he might serve as a warner to all people. This call was indeed universal, but since the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a resident of Makkah, his first confrontation had to be with the people of Makkah. Therefore it was the people of Makkah who rejected and opposed this call.

In short, blessed is He who sent down this Book upon His great servant, a Book that distinguishes between truth and falsehood and is a standard of truth.

Alladhi lahu mulku al-samawati… taqdira (25:2): "He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has taken no son, who has no partner in the dominion, who created everything and then determined it with due measure."

Here too, instead of using the Divine Name, the relative pronoun alladhi is used, meaning that the attributes being mentioned have a constant and continuous connection with Allah.

Alladhi lahu mulku al-samawati wa al-ard (25:2): "He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth." He has complete control over the heavens and the earth. They are in His possession. He fully disposes over them, and all changes within the heavens and the earth take place by His will and command.

Wa lam yattakhidh waladan (25:2): "He has not taken a son." Procreation is the natural law which Allah has established within His creation so that through it the continuity of "life" may be maintained. As for the Divine Being, since He is ever-enduring and everlasting, He has no need of the chain of procreation.

Wa lam yakun lahu shareekun fi al-mulk (25:2): "Nor has He any partner in the dominion." If one observes and analyzes the creation within the heavens and the earth, it will be found that its design was created by one single Creator. Within everything there is one law of power, and in all creation the working and the change are seen to belong to one single Being.

Wa khalaqa kulla shay'in faqaddarahu taqdira (25:2): "He created everything and then determined it with due measure." He determined its size and its form. He assigned it a task and a defined function. He determined its time and its place, and He harmonized it with the great existence of this universe.

Those scholars who have reflected upon the existence of this universe and the manner of its creation and composition, and every human being who ever reflects upon it, will be astonished. As the secrets hidden in the creation of the universe are unveiled, one becomes more and more certain that this universe did not come into existence by mere chance. Its composition is so fine and subtle that humans are incapable of even knowing its manifestations and effects, while we have so far observed only a small aspect of this universe. Yet as our discoveries advance, we find within this universe extremely wise governing laws. These laws are in harmony with this universe. The further our knowledge advances, the better we understand this verse.

Wa khalaqa kulla shay'in faqaddarahu taqdira (25:2): "He created everything and then determined it with a complete determination." Mr. A. Cressy Morrison, President of the New York Academy of Sciences, writes in his book "Man Does Not Stand Alone": "A person is overcome with astonishment when he reflects on the organization of this universe in its present form. It is an extremely wise arrangement. If the crust of the earth were a few steps thicker in proportion to its present size, plants and vegetation would have ceased to exist entirely."

"If the air were a little higher than its present position, the countless meteors that today burn up in the upper atmosphere would strike this terrestrial globe, because the speed of these meteors is 46 miles per second. Thus wherever they fell, they would burn whatever was capable of burning; and if their speed were reduced to the magnitude of a rifle bullet, they would all settle on the earth and stick, with terrible consequences. As for man, if even a small meteor passed near him whose speed is ninety times that of a rifle bullet, the heat of its mere passing would turn them into tiny dust."

"Allah has made this air to a specific density, and through this density pass those rays which have the effects on crops that they have, which kill germs and produce vitamins; but these rays do not harm man unless he remains in them beyond what is necessary. It is worth reflecting that poisonous gases are constantly emitted from the earth, yet the air, even under the continuous pollution of those gases, does not change the proportion that is necessary for human health. And it is these vast seas that maintain this balance, through which all kinds of life, food, moderate rain, habitation and vegetation receive life, and through which human life itself is sustained."

"At present oxygen in this air is 21 percent. If it were to increase to 50 percent, all material that is now capable of burning would catch fire entirely. A single spark would set the forests ablaze, and all the forests would explode in a flash. And if the oxygen in the air were to fall to 10 percent or lower, human life might, after centuries, adjust itself to this proportion, but human civilization would be deprived of many things it has today, for example fire and other energies."

"The regulation of these creatures and the natural balance within them is also extraordinary, so that no animal, however large its body and however clever it may be, is able to dominate this world."

"Indeed, man did this: by transferring plants and animals from one place to another, he tried to alter the balance that nature had established. And man received a severe punishment for this action, in that by disturbing this balance, animals, insects and plants had to face various diseases."

"The importance of this balance with respect to the existence of man can be well understood from the following incident. Some years ago in Australia a kind of thorny melon was cultivated. This cultivation was done as a protective hedge, but this crop spread so widely that within a short time it covered an area equal to England. It destroyed whole cities and the crops of the people were ruined, to the point that it became difficult for people to sow seed. People tried hard to control its spread, but it proved impossible. A danger arose for all of Australia that this thorny melon crop would take possession of it, and nothing was an obstacle to it."

"Entomologists spread throughout the world, began research, and eventually discovered an insect whose only food was this melon. This insect was also spreading at the same speed as the thorny melon. In Australia there was no natural obstacle to this insect either; it spread so widely that it reduced the thorny melon to nothing. As soon as the melon was destroyed, the insect too began to disappear. Only a very small quantity of it remained. It was as though nature had kept it in reserve against the spread of that melon. Thus did nature establish this arrangement to maintain order and balance."

"The question is: why did the malaria mosquito not dominate the whole world, such that our forefathers would have died from it, or that they would have acquired some means of protection against it? Similarly the same may be said of the yellow fever mosquito; in one season it advanced so far that it reached New York. Several kinds of mosquitoes are also found in the frozen sea. Likewise... the widespread extension of ... for what reasons did it not occur? It remained confined to its hot zones, and thus humanity was saved from the onslaught of its armies; otherwise human existence would have been wiped off the face of the earth. As for plague and other deadly epidemics and deadly germs, one may say that humanity itself had no medicines against these things until yesterday, so how did it survive? Moreover, until yesterday humanity was even ignorant of the basic principles of hygiene. So the survival of the human race in such circumstances is itself nothing short of a miracle."

"Then consider that insects do not have lungs of the kind that human beings have. These insects breathe through certain tubes that are within their bodies. When these insects grow beyond a certain size, not enough oxygen can enter through those tubes to suffice for their bodies. For this reason, no insect grows larger than a few inches. Likewise, the wings of these insects are also not very long. Within the system of creation and formation of these creeping things, they cannot grow beyond a certain measure. Thus the system of qadr (divine measure) has restrained their spreading. In this way, this world has been saved from their onslaught. If this principle of proportion had not been placed for the insects, then human survival on this earth would not have been possible. Just think about natural man: if a red fly the size of a lion's body, or a spider the size of a lion's body, were to come against him, could man confront such things?"

"There are also other miracles in the physical and natural structure of animals, such that if these natural arrangements for animals did not exist, no animal, nor even any plant, would exist in this world."

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 4–6:

(Wa qala alladhina kafaru... ghafooran raheema) (4 to 6) "" "".

This was the lie which the people of Quraysh attributed to the Prophet (ﷺ). Yet they knew well that it was a very great fabrication. For how could it remain hidden from the leaders of Quraysh, who taught the common people what they taught, that the Quran which Muhammad (ﷺ) recites is a speech entirely different from human modes of expression? They felt this deeply in their hearts, because they were well acquainted with human modes of speech. Whenever they heard the Quran, they themselves were greatly moved by it. Moreover, before the Prophethood, they had full certainty about Muhammad (ﷺ), that he was truthful and trustworthy. He neither told lies nor was he one who committed betrayal. How, then, is it possible that he would fabricate against Allah? That Allah had not said something, and Muhammad (ﷺ) should say that it is the word of Allah.

They made this accusation, on the one hand, out of obstinacy and stubbornness, and on the other hand, because these people held a kind of religious leadership in Makkah compared to other Arabs, and because of this they had a distinguished position among the Arabs. For this reason they spread this accusation among the common Arabs, because the common Arabs were not acquainted with modes of speech and could not distinguish between the Quran and ordinary speech. Therefore they would say:

(Inna hadha... qawmun akharun) (25:4) "This Furqan is a fabricated thing; he has invented it himself, and some other people have helped him in it." In the narrations, three or more non-Arab slaves are named, and by "qawmun akharun" (25:4) they used to point toward these people. How absurd was this statement! It was not even worthy of being discussed. The question is this: if this kind of speech could be produced with the help of a few non-Arab slaves, then why did they not produce a similar speech in response? In that way they could very easily have refuted the claim of Prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), especially when the Quran challenged them repeatedly, and they repeatedly failed to bring such speech.

For this reason, the Quran did not give any answer to this claim here, but rather refuted it clearly.

(Faqad ja'u zulman wa zooran) (25:4) "They have indeed come with a great injustice and a terrible lie." This is an injustice against the truth. They commit injustice against Muhammad (ﷺ), they commit injustice against their own selves. Their lie is evident and, at first glance, is falsehood, which does not even need refutation.

Further accusations against the Messenger (ﷺ) and the Quran

(Wa qalu... wa asila) (25:5) "They say: these are tales of the ancients which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening." The Quran has related the stories of earlier nations, for the sake of admonition, advice, training and guidance. Regarding these true stories, they say:

Asatir al-awwalin (25:5), that these are the stories of the ancient people, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told people to note them down so that they might be recited morning and evening. Because the Prophet (ﷺ) himself was unlettered and could not read or write, and the Prophet himself would then attribute these stories to God Almighty. The very basis of this claim contains their defeat, because their claim itself is baseless, so worthless that there is no need to discuss it. The manner in which the Quran presents its stories, the purposes for which they are brought, the reasoning drawn from them, the elegance with which they fulfill their aims, and the depth with which lofty objectives are established through them, are as far apart from old tales and stories as heaven is from earth. For old tales contain no thought or vision, nor do such stories have any purpose in view. Such stories are written and read merely for entertainment and for occupying one's leisure time, nothing more. (For details, see the chapter "Al-Qissah" in "Al-Tasweer al-Fanni fi al-Quran".)

They called the Quran "asatir al-awwalin" (25:5), indicating that these stories belong to very ancient times. Therefore, they assumed that those people must necessarily have been reading them to Muhammad (ﷺ), and they came to acquire knowledge of them. Therefore Allah refutes their accusation by saying that indeed its revelation upon Muhammad (ﷺ) is from the One who is more knowing than every possessor of knowledge. He is the knower of all secrets and mysteries, that is, Allah, and no knowledge of the first and the last is hidden from Him.

(Qul anzalahu alladhi ya'lamu al-sirra fi al-samawati wal-ard) (25:6) "Say, O Prophet (ﷺ): He has sent it down, who knows the secret of the heavens and the earth." What comparison is there between storytellers of this world and He who is All-Knowing and All-Aware? What is the limited knowledge of man compared with the complete and all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, who possesses the vast knowledge of the heavens and the earth? What comparison can a small drop have with a boundless ocean?

The truth is that these people are committing a great error when they level this baseless and worthless accusation against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while they believe in associating partners with Allah, although Allah has created them. Yet, despite this, the door of repentance is open, and they can turn away from this great sin. Allah, who knows the secrets of the heavens and the earths, is well aware of their fabrications and their plots, yet despite this He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. (Innahu kana ghafooran raheema) (25:6)

On this same subject the discussion moves further ahead. Their further objections against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), such as why he is a human being, and other vain demands, are set forth here.

How, then, is it possible that he would fabricate against Allah? That Allah had not said something, and Muhammad (ﷺ) should say that it is the word of Allah.

They made this accusation, on the one hand, out of obstinacy and stubbornness, and on the other hand, because these people held a kind of religious leadership in Makkah compared to other Arabs, and because of this they had a distinguished position among the Arabs. For this reason they spread this accusation among the common Arabs, because the common Arabs were not acquainted with modes of speech and could not distinguish between the Quran and ordinary speech. Therefore they would say:

(Inna hadha... qawmun akharun) (25:4) "This Furqan is a fabricated thing; he has invented it himself, and some other people have helped him in it." In the narrations, three or more non-Arab slaves are named, and by "qawmun akharun" (25:4) they used to point toward these people. How absurd was this statement! It was not even worthy of being discussed. The question is this: if this kind of speech could be produced with the help of a few non-Arab slaves, then why did they not produce a similar speech in response? In that way they could very easily have refuted the claim of Prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), especially when the Quran challenged them repeatedly, and they repeatedly failed to bring such speech.

For this reason, the Quran did not give any answer to this claim here, but rather refuted it clearly.

(Faqad ja'u zulman wa zooran) (25:4) "They have indeed come with a great injustice and a terrible lie." This is an injustice against the truth. They commit injustice against Muhammad (ﷺ), they commit injustice against their own selves. Their lie is evident and, at first glance, is falsehood, which does not even need refutation.

Further accusations against the Messenger (ﷺ) and the Quran

(Wa qalu... wa asila) (25:5) "They say: these are tales of the ancients which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening." The Quran has related the stories of earlier nations, for the sake of admonition, advice, training and guidance. Regarding these true stories, they say:

Asatir al-awwalin (25:5), that these are the stories of the ancient people, and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told people to note them down so that they might be recited morning and evening. Because the Prophet (ﷺ) himself was unlettered and could not read or write, and the Prophet himself would then attribute these stories to God Almighty. The very basis of this claim contains their defeat, because their claim itself is baseless, so worthless that there is no need to discuss it. The manner in which the Quran presents its stories, the purposes for which they are brought, the reasoning drawn from them, the elegance with which they fulfill their aims, and the depth with which lofty objectives are established through them, are as far apart from old tales and stories as heaven is from earth. For old tales contain no thought or vision, nor do such stories have any purpose in view. Such stories are written and read merely for entertainment and for occupying one's leisure time, nothing more. (For details, see the chapter "Al-Qissah" in "Al-Tasweer al-Fanni fi al-Quran".)

They called the Quran "asatir al-awwalin" (25:5), indicating that these stories belong to very ancient times. Therefore, they assumed that those people must necessarily have been reading them to Muhammad (ﷺ), and they came to acquire knowledge of them. Therefore Allah refutes their accusation by saying that indeed its revelation upon Muhammad (ﷺ) is from the One who is more knowing than every possessor of knowledge. He is the knower of all secrets and mysteries, that is, Allah, and no knowledge of the first and the last is hidden from Him.

(Qul anzalahu alladhi ya'lamu al-sirra fi al-samawati wal-ard) (25:6) "Say, O Prophet (ﷺ): He has sent it down, who knows the secret of the heavens and the earth." What comparison is there between storytellers of this world and He who is All-Knowing and All-Aware? What is the limited knowledge of man compared with the complete and all-encompassing knowledge of Allah, who possesses the vast knowledge of the heavens and the earth? What comparison can a small drop have with a boundless ocean?

The truth is that these people are committing a great error when they level this baseless and worthless accusation against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), while they believe in associating partners with Allah, although Allah has created them. Yet, despite this, the door of repentance is open, and they can turn away from this great sin. Allah, who knows the secrets of the heavens and the earths, is well aware of their fabrications and their plots, yet despite this He is Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. (Innahu kana ghafooran raheema) (25:6)

On this same subject the discussion moves further ahead. Their further objections against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), such as why he is a human being, and other vain demands, are set forth here.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 7–8:

(*Wa qalu ma lahadha...* to *...qusuran*) (7–10)

"What kind of Messenger is this, who eats and drinks, walks about in the markets, and conducts all his affairs like human beings?" This is the same worn-out objection that people have always raised against the messengers: "So-and-so has claimed to be a messenger. Look, brother, so-and-so's son has now become a messenger too. He is just a human being like us, who eats, drinks and walks about as we do." They also ask: "How can it be that he is the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and that revelation (*wahy*) comes to him from Allah? How is it possible for him to be connected with, and in contact with, the higher realm (*'alam-i-bala*), and to receive guidance from the higher realm, when he is a human being made of the same flesh and bone as us? Why does revelation not come to us? And why does the knowledge he claims not come to us, when there is nothing distinctive between us and this Messenger?"

From one angle, this matter does indeed appear strange and puzzling. But from another angle it is natural and reasonable. Allah breathed His own spirit into man, and it is because of that spirit that man became a human being, and it is for that reason that Allah entrusted him with the vicegerency (*khilafah*) on earth, even though man possesses limited knowledge, his experience is limited, and he has very few resources. It was therefore not possible that Allah would leave man alone and unsupported to discharge this great duty, and leave him without guidance and direction. Moreover, Allah has also placed within him the capacity to establish a connection with the higher realm. Therefore, it is not surprising that Allah should choose one human being from among mankind for this purpose, so that he may receive the guidance of the higher realm and convey it to the people. And Allah gives this person special capacity for this purpose, so that whenever any matter becomes doubtful for them, he may resolve it in the light of Allah's guidance, and whenever they need help in adopting the path of guidance, he may assist them.

This is a great honour for man, in this respect and in this form. Yet some people do not understand this honour, nor do they value this dignity and esteem of man. Therefore, those in whose minds this matter does not settle deny this honour, asking how any person among men could be a messenger. They argue that for this purpose an angel would have been more suitable than human beings.

(*Law la unzila...* to *...nadhira*) (25:7): ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him, to walk along with him and warn [the disbelievers]?﴾ Yet Allah had commanded all the angels to prostrate before Adam, because Allah had honoured man on account of certain of his qualities, and these qualities arose from the spirituality breathed into man from the higher realm.

Furthermore, there is another wisdom in sending a human being as a messenger to human beings. A human being has human feelings and human tastes. His experiences are also like those of other human beings. By virtue of being human, he can understand their pains and sorrows and their desires. He can also understand their emotions and inclinations. He is aware of the needs of human beings and of their responsibilities. Therefore, he takes into account their weaknesses and shortcomings, and he is hopeful about their strength and their capacities, and he moves forward with them step by step. He is thoroughly aware of their impressions and their reactions, because he is one of them. He has been sent for their guidance and direction, and he guides them with the guidance and help of Allah.

Moreover, it is also possible for these people to follow Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), because he is a human being like them. He moves forward gradually with these people. By living among them, he presents a moral model, and he teaches them practically the morals and duties that Allah has imposed upon them and which Allah requires of them. Thus he is a model of the doctrine and practice that he presents to the people. His life, his deeds and all his movements are an open book, which he presents before them, and they copy each and every line of that book. They give reality to every single word of that book, and they see that their Messenger presents every matter in practice, so they also imitate him, because this doctrine and guidance is visibly manifest in the life of one person. If the Messenger were an angel, people could neither observe his deeds nor think of imitating him, because from the very beginning it would have been in their minds that "he is an angel, this is his nature, and we are weak human beings. How can we adopt conduct like his? Or how can we imitate him? Or how can we present a model like him?"

This was the wisdom of Allah, who created everything and made it in perfect proportion. It was His wisdom that He sent a human being as a Messenger for the guidance of mankind, so that he might lead them. The objection to the Messenger being a human being arises in fact from ignorance of this wisdom. Moreover, in it there is also an honouring of man by Allah, and those who raise this objection deny the dignity of man.

Their second objection was even more simple-minded and ignorant than the first: that this Messenger walks about in the bazaars, obtains the things he needs, and works. So why did Allah not give him so much wealth that he would be free of concern for his needs, and that his needs would be met without any labour?

(*Aw yulqa ilayhi kanzun...*) (25:8): ﴿Or why was not a treasure bestowed upon him, or why does he not have a garden from which he could eat?﴾ Allah did not wish that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) should possess a treasure, or that he should be the owner of a great garden, because Allah was making him a model for His community, so that he would carry out the duties of the office of prophethood, and alongside those duties he would also bear his own responsibilities as a human being, just like the other human beings of his community. He would strive himself for his sustenance, so that no one in the community could object that this man is conducting some trade. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was a man of contentment (*qana'ah*). Therefore, he did not have to struggle very hard for the necessities of life. That is why he was free to carry out the duties of conveying the message of prophethood, and no obstacle arose for him in this matter. Accordingly, he strove for his needs only to the extent necessary, and he also discharged the duties of prophethood, so that every member of his community, taking him as a model, might assume a share of the duty of conveying the message of prophethood, and also strive for their own needs.

In later periods, a flood of wealth flowed at the feet of the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah tested the life of His Messenger in this respect too, so that this aspect also might be a model for the people. Accordingly, he never paid attention to that flood of wealth. He (ﷺ) was generous like a windstorm. Thus he (ﷺ) also overcame the temptation of wealth, and in this way he removed the greed for riches from people's hearts. This was so that people could not object: "Muhammad (ﷺ) set out with a message, he was a poor man, he had no financial activity, and no financial standing, and now he is playing with millions and billions. Wealth is raining down upon him from every direction." But the Prophet (ﷺ) kept this flood of wealth away from himself as well, and he remained engaged in the work of the Islamic call just as he had been engaged in it during the period of poverty.

What is wealth, and what is the reality of treasures? What is the value of gardens? When a weak and mortal human being attains access to God, then for him the entire earth and all that is in it has no worth. Rather, in his estimation, the whole creation living in this universe has no worth. But he reaches this state only when he has attained access to the Creator of the universe, who bestows abundance and scarcity. At that time, however, people were unable to grasp this reality.

(*Wa qalaz-zalimuna...*) (25:8): ﴿And the wrongdoers say: "You are only following a man who has been bewitched."﴾ This is the unjust statement that Allah has quoted from the mouths of these people. Allah has also quoted this accusation of theirs word for word in Surah Al-Isra. There Allah gave this reply:

(25:9): ﴿See how they coin comparisons for you; so they have gone astray, and they cannot find a way.﴾ The theme and subject of this Surah and of Surah Al-Isra are one and the same, and the matter in both Surahs is being discussed in the same context. In both places these people raised this objection; they attacked the person of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and found fault with him personally. That is, they were persuading people that this man's reason has been destroyed, because he speaks strange and wonderful things, and an ordinary normal person does not speak like this. But through this objection, it escaped their subconscious mind that the things the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) says are not ordinary matters. Generally, not even the greatest intellectual speaks in such a way. These are matters beyond human power. Therefore, when refuting them, Allah confined Himself to expressing astonishment at their attitude.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 11–16:

(Nay, they denied... ...a blazing fire) (11) ...and a promise they have asked for.

That is, they have crossed the limits of disbelief and error and reached the point where they deny the Day of Judgment. The Qur'an's mode of expression, by using the word "bal" (nay/rather), presents their misguidance as though they have gone very far along this path: leave aside the earlier matters, for they have already denied the Hereafter. After this, it is revealed how terrible a punishment has been prepared for these troublemakers. It is a fire that stands ready, kindled and blazing.

﴿And We have prepared for him who denies the Hour a blazing fire﴾ (25:11). Here the Qur'an presents the fire in an embodied and personified manner. Personification (tajsim and tashkhis) is the Qur'anic style in which things, meanings and concepts that cannot in reality be alive are presented in the manner of living beings. Thus the Qur'an presents concepts and scenes in the form of living persons, so that a supreme degree of inimitability arises within the speech.

Consider it. We stand before a blazing fire. This fire takes on the form of a living, wrathful being: it sees those deniers from afar. Upon seeing them, the fire is seized with rage and fury, and these people perceive from afar its expression of anger and its harsh roar, as though it charges at them from a distance, boiling with the passion of vengeance, while these people are still on the way and have not yet arrived. In short, this is an extremely shaking scene, at which the legs of the onlookers begin to tremble.

Now see, it has reached its destination. These people are not left free to struggle with the fire with their hands and feet, so that the fire overcomes them, nor to try to escape while it seizes them. Rather, they are seized and cast into it, with their hands and feet bound in chains. They are not thrown into an open hall of fire, but are confined in an extremely narrow place within the fire of Hell, where they can barely fit, and there is no way out of it. Now these people have become utterly hopeless of being freed from this fire, and they are in extreme anguish. Having despaired, they can only call upon destruction and death.

﴿And when they are cast into it, in a narrow place, bound together, they will call out for destruction there﴾ (25:13). But in Hell, the wish for death is an unfulfilled desire, since they can be freed from this torment only through death, because this agony is unbearable. Yet their request and this wish are answered with mockery and derision, just as they used to mock the Messengers. It is a bitter mockery.

﴿Do not call out today for one destruction; call out for many destructions﴾ (25:14). For the destruction of a single time will not benefit you, nor will one death suffice for you. You will die again and again, and you will be raised again and again.

After presenting their state, a glimpse of the end of the God-fearing believers, who feared Allah, who hoped to present themselves before Allah, and who had firm faith in the Day of Judgment, is also shown in contrast. This end too is presented, addressing these disbelievers, in a highly sarcastic manner.

﴿Say: Is that better, or the everlasting Garden which has been promised to the God-fearing, which will be their recompense and their final destination...﴾ (25:15–16) ﴿For them therein is whatever they wish, abiding forever; it is a promise binding upon your Lord to be fulfilled﴾. Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 17–19:

﴿And on the day He gathers them and what they worship besides Allah, He will say, "Was it you who misled these My servants, or did they stray from the way themselves?"﴾ (25:17) Those whom the polytheists used to worship were sometimes idols, sometimes angels and jinn, and sometimes other deities. Allah knows them well. But to question them in this open plain, when all have been gathered for this very purpose, is for greater exposure and humiliation. Exposing a crime and causing shame is in itself a kind of punishment. The answer that follows shows that these so-called deities stand in complete submission before Allah. Now they stand as obedient subjects before Allah, the Subduer, the Owner of the kingdom. Not only do they deny their own divinity, but they also deny that there was any friendship or connection between them and those foolish worshippers. What greater humiliation could there be for the polytheists than that those whom they consider gods should disown their relationship with them?

﴿They will say, "Glory be to You! It was not for us to take any protectors besides You. But You granted them and their fathers enjoyment until they forgot the reminder, and they became a people doomed to ruin."﴾ (25:18) The worshippers were given a lifetime of provisions, continuously, without recognising that there is a Giver of these blessings, and without giving thanks to the Giver. This heedlessness removed from their hearts any awareness of these favours. These people forgot everything. Thus their hearts became dry and barren, just as land becomes barren and waterless through drought. The word *bawār* (ruin) is used here, which carries the meaning of destruction. But along with destruction, its meaning includes drought and barrenness as well, that is, the dryness of hearts and the emptiness of life.

Here, they are shamed with a humiliating address:

﴿Then they will deny you in what you say, so you will be able to avert neither [punishment] nor help.﴾ (25:19) That is, they will be unable to turn this calamity away from themselves, nor will they receive any help from anywhere.

This scene belongs to the Hereafter and the plain of gathering, but in between, a glimpse of the world is also shown. These deniers now appear, in this very world, upon the earth, and they are addressed:

﴿And whoever among you wrongs, We will make him taste a great punishment.﴾ (25:19) It is a distinctive style of the Qur'an that it touches hearts at the moment when they are ready to accept, and when, having seen the terrifying scene of the Day of Resurrection, they are inclined to accept the truth.
