Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 25, verse 20:

Now, when they and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw that these people had gone to the extreme of slander, denial and mockery, and had even raised objections to the humanity of the Messenger (ﷺ), to his walking in the markets and to his eating and drinking, the address turns towards the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He is consoled, and with sympathy for him it is said that he is not the only messenger about whom these people are astonished. Rather, all the messengers were like this, just as you are, and their circumstances were also like yours.

﴿And We did not send before you any messengers but that they ate food and walked in the markets. And We have made some of you a trial for others. Will you be patient? And your Lord is ever Seeing.﴾ If these people are raising objections, they are not objecting to your person. They are objecting to a practice of Allah (sunnah) and a constant method of His. This method is fixed, determined and defined, and it has a definite outcome.

﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others﴾ (25:20). In reality, We have made you a means of trial for one another, so that those who do not know the wisdom and planning of Allah continue to object, while those who fear Allah, and know His wisdom and His dispositions, remain patient, and so that the Islamic call prevails, and that it confronts the dominance (of falsehood), and advances using human resources in this confrontation and struggle. Whoever remains steadfast in this struggle will succeed.

﴿Will you be patient?﴾ (25:20), that is, will you endure difficulties with patience?

﴿And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾ (25:20). He observes the temperament of all people, sees all hearts, and has knowledge of the circumstances and outcome of all people. You will receive your full reward.

In ﴿And your Lord﴾ (25:20), Allah addresses Himself as the Lord of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This manner of expression has a deep effect on the heart. The heart is refreshed, it is consoled and finds tranquility, and it becomes ready to strive anew. The impression given is: O Muhammad, We are watching, We are with you, do not worry. Not only are outward circumstances within Our sight, but even the most hidden matters and what is in the hearts are within Our sight. Through this manner of expression, Allah brings Himself close to His servants.

This lesson opens in the same manner as the previous lesson, and its theme proceeds in the same way; however, here the objections of the polytheists are directed at the Lord, the Exalted. Here they raise objections against Allah and prescribe for Him their own course of action. In other words, in this lesson they advance further in their arrogance: while objecting to the Messenger of Allah, they proceed to object against God Himself. This too is a way of consoling and encouraging the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, showing that they do not object to you alone, but their insolence extends even into the presence of Allah. Here, however, instead of giving a direct answer, they are swiftly shown glimpses of some of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection. And this is the fitting response to their insolence. Their insolence was this:

﴿Why are not the angels sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?﴾ (25:21)

After this, their further objection is quoted: why was the Qur'an revealed in installments (piecemeal)? An answer is given to this, and it is explained why the Qur'an was revealed continuously in parts. The Messenger is comforted, with the assurance that whenever they bring forth an argument, We also provide you with a new explanation and the best interpretation and clarification. After this, for the consideration of the Prophet and his opponents, a picture is also drawn of the time when some of the deniers were destroyed, and how these nations were annihilated. Just consider the ruins of the people of Lot; you pass by them day and night. The Qur'an seizes them sharply, because when they see those ruins day and night, their hearts are not affected in the least. All these matters have been brought in order that the objections they used to raise against the person of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ may be stated here in one place. After presenting these events, a forceful comment is made upon them. In it, their most contemptible picture is drawn, in a most realistic manner:

﴿Nay, they are but like cattle; rather, they are further astray﴾ (25:44)

﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say...﴾ (25:21) to ﴿...a forsaker for man﴾ (25:29)

The polytheists do not expect to meet Us, nor do they await it, nor do they give it any importance, nor do they order their lives and their activities according to this belief. Therefore, in their hearts there is neither fear of Allah, nor love and reverence for Him. For this reason, such words come from their tongues regarding Allah which could never come from the tongue of one who fears God.

﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say, "Why are not the angels sent down to us, or [why] do we not see our Lord?"﴾ (25:21)

They considered it improbable that a messenger could be a human being. Therefore they demanded that an angel should descend and bear witness to the creed to which they were being invited, or that they themselves should see the Lord with their own eyes and confirm it. This is in truth an encroachment upon the station and rank of Allah, and a demand of an ignorant and rebellious person who has no awareness of the dignity of the Lord of the worlds and does not honour Allah as He should be honoured. Who are these insolent people, and what is their standing before Allah, who is Exalted, Mighty and Great? What standing do they have in His vast dominion and in this great universe? Their status is that of a trivial particle. Man's standing in this universe is established only when he connects himself with Allah and increases his weight through faith, thereby creating some value for himself. Therefore, before concluding this verse, Allah Himself tells us the cause of this insolence.

﴿Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed greatly in insolence﴾ (25:21)

In their own estimation they are very great. Therefore they are engrossed in arrogance, and because of this arrogance they are involved in a very great rebellion. They are so intoxicated with themselves that they cannot weigh true values correctly. Now the habit of these people is that they perceive only their own selves. Their self is so great a thing in their eyes that in this universe they consider only their own selves to be significant: so great that even Allah, Glorified be His Majesty, should appear before it, so that they may see Him, confirm Him, and believe in Him.

Instead of answering their question, Allah, by way of mockery and derision, presents before them a picture of their misfortune and helplessness, and it is said that when on the Day of Resurrection they see the angels (seeing the angels was also one of their demands), then on that day evil will befall them. Their condition will be that the punishment that cannot be averted will stand before them; they will see no way of escape from it, and this will be the day of punishment and recompense.

﴿On the day they see the angels, there will be no good news that Day for the criminals; and they will say, "A forbidding forbidden."﴾ (25:22)

﴿And We will proceed to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ (25:23)

On the day this demand of theirs is fulfilled and the angels appear before them, they will see the angels. But on that day there will be no good tidings for them; rather, there will be news of punishment for them. Thus their demand will be fulfilled in a strange manner. On that day they will speak thus: ﴿A forbidding forbidden﴾ (25:22), meaning "God forbid!" This was a phrase used to ward off evil and was said to enemies, invoking their destruction and seeking protection from their harm. This expression will escape their tongues in the Resurrection, just as in the world they used to utter it to seek refuge from evil. Today, how can they obtain the protection of God? Even if they seek the protection of God a million times today, it will benefit them nothing.

﴿And We will proceed to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ (25:23)

This process will be completed in an instant. All their deeds will be blown away like dust. Observe the manner of expression: our imagination sees it as a personal, embodied being coming and carrying off their deeds and scattering them like dust. This is the Qur'an's manner of embodiment and imagery. The meaning is that whatever they had gathered in the world in the form of righteous deeds will be reduced to dust. And this is because their deeds were not based on faith. Through faith alone does a person reach Allah. Faith gives righteous deeds a method, firmness and continuity, and these deeds have a purpose and a direction. They do not proceed from some momentary impulse, nor are they the running about of a person who knows no right path or direction, moving aimlessly here and there, or mere purposeless exertion. In Islam, no righteous deed has any value if it has no defined direction, no purpose, and no spirit, for such deeds bring no benefit at all.

The existence of man in this universe, his deeds, and the striving of his life are in fact connected with the reality of this universe. Man too is a part of the law of nature, and this entire universe is connected with the Divine Being. Man and all his activities are included in it. If man's striving, movement and exertion are cut off from this true light, they become purposeless. They are lost, and they have no weight or value before Allah. His deeds will have no reckoning, and they will have no value; rather, in the Islamic view, his existence is not even considered as such. He is merely wind and dust.

Faith brings man to the Lord. Thus, before the Lord of the worlds, his deeds also acquire weight, and a reckoning is kept for him in the account of this universe, and his deeds are displayed in the construction and progress of this universe. Since these polytheists have no faith, their deeds are rendered null and void. Yet the Qur'an has adopted a most concrete and sensory manner of expression.

﴿And We will proceed to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ (25:23)

And let us also consider the condition of the believers, for comparison. These are the people of Paradise.

﴿The companions of Paradise will be, that Day, in a better dwelling place and a finer resting place at noon﴾ (25:24)

They will dwell in great comfort, joy and stability, in deep shade. The word "dwelling" (mustaqarr) is used here in contrast to the immaturity of the deeds of the disbelievers and their scattering like dust in the air, and the rest and tranquility of midday stands in opposition to it. In contrast with the disbelievers' lamentation and helplessness, when they will seek the protection of God and say, ﴿A forbidding forbidden﴾ (25:22)...

The disbelievers used to make this demand of the Prophet ﷺ: that Allah should come before them in the shade of clouds, and that the angels should accompany him. They used to make these demands having heard the stories of the Children of Israel, according to which Allah descends in the shade of clouds, or in the form of a column of fire. Therefore, the Qur'an presents, in another manner, a scene of the fulfilment of their demand on the Day of Resurrection, when the angels will descend.

﴿And the Day the sky will be split apart with clouds, and the angels will be sent down, descending in a stately manner. The sovereignty that Day will be truly for the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.﴾ (25:25–26)

This verse, along with countless other verses of the Qur'an, shows that on that Day there will be enormous cosmic events and catastrophes. All such verses point to the fact that this universe which we see, and this system which we see, will all be thrown into disorder. All its heavens, its planets and stars will collide with one another. The order of this universe, the mutual relations of things, and the present form of everything will change, and this upheaval will be the end of this world. This cosmic revolution will not be limited to the earth; all the stars, all the heavens and all the planets will be affected by it. It is appropriate here to present some scenes of this revolution, which have come in several surahs.

﴿When the sun is wrapped up, when the stars fall, when the mountains are set moving, and when the seas are set boiling﴾ (81:1–3, 6)

﴿When the sky is split open, when the stars are scattered, when the seas are burst forth, and when the graves are turned upside down﴾ (82:1–4)

﴿When the sky splits asunder, and it listens to its Lord and is required to do so; and when the earth is stretched out and casts out what is within it and empties itself, and listens to its Lord and is required to do so﴾ (84:1–5)

﴿When the earth is pounded to powder, and the mountains become like scattered dust﴾ (56:4–6)

﴿Then when the Trumpet is blown with one blast, and the earth and the mountains are lifted and crushed with a single blow, on that Day the Event will occur﴾ (69:13–16)

﴿The Day the sky will be like molten silver, and the mountains will be like wool, carded﴾ (70:8–9)

﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake, and the earth brings forth its burdens﴾ (99:1–2)

﴿The Day when mankind will be like scattered moths, and the mountains like wool, fluffed up﴾ (101:4–5)

﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke that will envelop the people. This is a painful punishment﴾ (44:10–11)

﴿The Day the earth and the mountains will quake, and the mountains will become heaps of sand, poured out﴾ (73:14)

﴿The sky will be split asunder by it﴾ (73:18)

﴿No! When the earth is leveled, pounded to powder﴾ (89:21)

﴿So when vision is dazzled, and the moon darkens, and the sun and moon are joined﴾ (75:7–9)

﴿So when the stars are dimmed, and the sky is split open, and the mountains are blown away﴾ (77:8–10)

﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away as dust, and leave the earth a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or unevenness"﴾ (20:105–107)

﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them fixed, while they will pass away as clouds pass﴾ (27:88)

﴿And the Day We set the mountains in motion, and you will see the earth laid bare﴾ (18:47)

﴿On the Day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens as well﴾ (14:48)

﴿On the Day when We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for writings﴾ (21:104). All these verses show that the end of this world of ours will be extremely terrifying. The earth will be struck violently, the great celestial bodies will collide with one another with a thunderous crash, and the mountains will be crushed to dust and scattered. The seas will burst forth, either because of the upheavals of the earth's crust or because the particles of the seas will split apart, and through radiation the waters will catch fire. Bright stars will lose their light. The sky will split open and be torn into pieces. The stars and planets will collide with one another, be crushed, and scatter. All the vast distances of the heavens will vanish. The sun and moon will be joined together. At times the sky will be like black smoke, and at times like the flame of a fire. In short, it will be a dreadful hour, and in it a person will be overcome with terror.

In such a situation, Allah tells the polytheists, by way of warning, that on that Day a cloud will appear splitting the sky, and on that Day the rows of angels will be sent down upon the disbelievers, just as they had demanded. They did not make this demand in order to confirm Muhammad (ﷺ). These angels will come by the command of Allah, bringing the punishment of Allah.

﴿And that Day will be a hard day for the disbelievers﴾ (25:26). Because on that Day a severe punishment will be before them, it will be a terrifying day. These people demand the descent of the angels out of ignorance, whereas the angels come bringing punishment.

After this, one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection is brought forward. In it, these misguided and wrongdoing people will be deeply ashamed. This scene is very long, so long that the spectators think it will go on forever. This wrongdoer is biting his own hands out of extreme remorse and regret.

﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way. Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend. He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter."﴾ (25:27–29)

This person is expressing deep regret, and silence has fallen over his surroundings. This person keeps raising his regretful voice. His cries are so heart-rending, and their effect so long-lasting, that the assembly keeps growing longer, and the impressions become ever deeper. Even today, a reader of these verses is seized by deep regret, and those who witness the scene become sharers in the grief.

﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾ (25:27). It is not only one hand that he will bite but both hands, now this one and now that one. Because of the intensity of his grief, he will vent his anger upon his own hands. The biting of the hands points to what the psychological state of the wrongdoer will be on that Day. His sorrow and anguish have been expressed through an embodied action and movement, meaning that he will be unable to bear the grief.

﴿He will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way"﴾ (25:27). That is, I wish I had followed the way of the Messenger of Allah, and had not separated myself from the Messenger, whose prophethood he had denied, on the grounds that this Messenger is a human being.

﴿Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend﴾ (25:28). Here "so-and-so" is used generally, without naming anyone, so that all misguiding companions are included: every friend who leads friends toward error. However, the narrations state that the occasion of revelation of these verses was ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt. This man used to sit and rise very frequently with the Prophet (ﷺ). He invited the Prophet (ﷺ) to a feast, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said that he would not accept his invitation until he bore witness to two things. So he did so. Ubayy ibn Khalaf was also his friend, and he greatly shamed him, saying, "You have become irreligious." He replied, "By Allah, I have not accepted the religion of Muhammad." But he (Ubayy) said, "I will not accept your invitation until you utter the shahadah." Yet they (Muhammad and his companions) were in my house and did not eat my food. I felt very ashamed that he should not eat my food, so I recited the shahadah. Then Ubayy ibn Khalaf said, "By Allah, I will not be pleased with you unless you go and spit in his face, grasping his neck." The Prophet (ﷺ) was found prostrating in Dar al-Nadwah (the council house of Quraysh), and that wretched man did exactly this. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him that whenever he met him outside Makkah, he would cut off his head. This man was taken prisoner on the day of Badr, and the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) to cut off his neck.

﴿He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me﴾ (25:29). It was in fact Satan who was leading him astray, or was a helper of Satan.

﴿And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter﴾ (25:29). He brings the human being to the end of shame, and when the time of truth comes, Satan always runs away, especially in dreadful and anguishing scenes and occasions.

Thus the Qur'an shook the hearts of these people. It presented before them their end in the form of scenes that make one tremble, as though it were an event being witnessed before their eyes, even though those people are still upon this earth, denying Allah, rejecting with great contempt the prospect of appearing before Allah, and making demands that are foolish. Yet they are about to face an extremely terrifying situation there, and will be overwhelmed by utmost shame and remorse, but at that time remorse will be of no benefit.

Now the discourse turns from the scenes of the Day of Resurrection back to this world. The position they have taken regarding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is discussed. Now their objection is why the Qur'an was not revealed all at once. The present manner of the revelation of the Qur'an is objectionable to them. This question and answer also concludes with a scene of the Resurrection: just as their objection is reversed, so too they will be dragged upside down into Hell.

In such a situation, Allah tells the polytheists, by way of warning, that on that Day a cloud will appear splitting the sky, and on that Day the rows of angels will be sent down upon the disbelievers, just as they had demanded. They did not make this demand in order to confirm Muhammad (ﷺ). These angels will come by the command of Allah, bringing the punishment of Allah.

﴿And that Day will be a hard day for the disbelievers﴾ (25:26). Because on that Day a severe punishment will be before them, it will be a terrifying day. These people demand the descent of the angels out of ignorance, whereas the angels come bringing punishment.

After this, one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection is brought forward. In it, these misguided and wrongdoing people will be deeply ashamed. This scene is very long, so long that the spectators think it will go on forever. This wrongdoer is biting his own hands out of extreme remorse and regret.

﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way. Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend. He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter."﴾ (25:27–29)

This person is expressing deep regret, and silence has fallen over his surroundings. This person keeps raising his regretful voice. His cries are so heart-rending, and their effect so long-lasting, that the assembly keeps growing longer, and the impressions become ever deeper. Even today, a reader of these verses is seized by deep regret, and those who witness the scene become sharers in the grief.

﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾ (25:27). It is not only one hand that he will bite but both hands, now this one and now that one. Because of the intensity of his grief, he will vent his anger upon his own hands. The biting of the hands points to what the psychological state of the wrongdoer will be on that Day. His sorrow and anguish have been expressed through an embodied action and movement, meaning that he will be unable to bear the grief.

﴿Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend﴾ (25:28). Here "so-and-so" is used generally, without naming anyone, so that all misguiding companions are included: every friend who leads friends toward error. However, the narrations state that the occasion of revelation of these verses was ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt. This man used to sit and rise very frequently with the Prophet (ﷺ). He invited the Prophet (ﷺ) to a feast, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said that he would not accept his invitation until he bore witness to two things. So he did so. Ubayy ibn Khalaf was also his friend, and he greatly shamed him, saying, "You have become irreligious." He replied, "By Allah, I have not accepted the religion of Muhammad." It presented before them their end in the form of scenes that make one tremble, as though it were an event being witnessed before their eyes, even though those people are still upon this earth, denying Allah, rejecting with great contempt the prospect of appearing before Allah, and making demands that are foolish. Yet they are about to face an extremely terrifying situation there, and will be overwhelmed by utmost shame and remorse, but at that time remorse will be of no benefit.

This question and answer also concludes with a scene of the Resurrection: just as their objection is reversed, so too they will be dragged upside down into Hell.

Therefore, before concluding this verse, Allah Himself tells us the cause of this insolence.

﴿Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed greatly in insolence﴾ (25:21)

In their own estimation they are very great. Therefore they are engrossed in arrogance, and because of this arrogance they are involved in a very great rebellion. They are so intoxicated with themselves that they cannot weigh true values correctly. Now the habit of these people is that they perceive only their own selves. Their self is so great a thing in their eyes that in this universe they consider only their own selves to be significant: so great that even Allah, Glorified be His Majesty, should appear before it, so that they may see Him, confirm Him, and believe in Him.

Their condition will be that the punishment that cannot be averted will stand before them; they will see no way of escape from it, and this will be the day of punishment and recompense.

﴿On the day they see the angels, there will be no good news that Day for the criminals; and they will say, "A forbidding forbidden."﴾ (25:22)

On the day this demand of theirs is fulfilled and the angels appear before them, they will see the angels. This was a phrase used to ward off evil and was said to enemies, invoking their destruction and seeking protection from their harm. This expression will escape their tongues in the Resurrection, just as in the world they used to utter it to seek refuge from evil. Today, how can they obtain the protection of God? Even if they seek the protection of God a million times today, it will benefit them nothing.

This process will be completed in an instant. All their deeds will be blown away like dust. Faith gives righteous deeds a method, firmness and continuity, and these deeds have a purpose and a direction. They do not proceed from some momentary impulse, nor are they the running about of a person who knows no right path or direction, moving aimlessly here and there, or mere purposeless exertion. In Islam, no righteous deed has any value if it has no defined direction, no purpose, and no spirit, for such deeds bring no benefit at all.

If man's striving, movement and exertion are cut off from this true light, they become purposeless. They are lost, and they have no weight or value before Allah. His deeds will have no reckoning, and they will have no value; rather, in the Islamic view, his existence is not even considered as such. He is merely wind and dust.

Faith brings man to the Lord. Thus, before the Lord of the worlds, his deeds also acquire weight, and a reckoning is kept for him in the account of this universe, and his deeds are displayed in the construction and progress of this universe. Since these polytheists have no faith, their deeds are rendered null and void. Yet the Qur'an has adopted a most concrete and sensory manner of expression.

And let us also consider the condition of the believers, for comparison. These are the people of Paradise.

﴿The companions of Paradise will be, that Day, in a better dwelling place and a finer resting place at noon﴾ (25:24)

They will dwell in great comfort, joy and stability, in deep shade. The word "dwelling" (mustaqarr) is used here in contrast to the immaturity of the deeds of the disbelievers and their scattering like dust in the air, and the rest and tranquility of midday stands in opposition to it. In contrast with the disbelievers' lamentation and helplessness, when they will seek the protection of God and say, ﴿A forbidding forbidden﴾ (25:22)...

The disbelievers used to make this demand of the Prophet ﷺ: that Allah should come before them in the shade of clouds, and that the angels should accompany him. They used to make these demands having heard the stories of the Children of Israel, according to which Allah descends in the shade of clouds, or in the form of a column of fire. This verse, along with countless other verses of the Qur'an, shows that on that Day there will be enormous cosmic events and catastrophes. All such verses point to the fact that this universe which we see, and this system which we see, will all be thrown into disorder. All its heavens, its planets and stars will collide with one another. The order of this universe, the mutual relations of things, and the present form of everything will change, and this upheaval will be the end of this world. This cosmic revolution will not be limited to the earth; all the stars, all the heavens and all the planets will be affected by it. ﴿When the earth is shaken with its [final] earthquake, and the earth brings forth its burdens﴾ (99:1–2)

﴿The Day when mankind will be like scattered moths, and the mountains like wool, fluffed up﴾ (101:4–5)

﴿So watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke that will envelop the people. This is a painful punishment﴾ (44:10–11)

﴿The Day the earth and the mountains will quake, and the mountains will become heaps of sand, poured out﴾ (73:14)

﴿The sky will be split asunder by it﴾ (73:18)

﴿No! When the earth is leveled, pounded to powder﴾ (89:21)

﴿So when vision is dazzled, and the moon darkens, and the sun and moon are joined﴾ (75:7–9)

﴿So when the stars are dimmed, and the sky is split open, and the mountains are blown away﴾ (77:8–10)

﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away as dust, and leave the earth a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or unevenness"﴾ (20:105–107)

The earth will be struck violently, the great celestial bodies will collide with one another with a thunderous crash, and the mountains will be crushed to dust and scattered. The seas will burst forth, either because of the upheavals of the earth's crust or because the particles of the seas will split apart, and through radiation the waters will catch fire. All its heavens, its planets and stars will collide with one another. The order of this universe, the mutual relations of things, and the present form of everything will change, and this upheaval will be the end of this world. The earth will be struck violently, the great celestial bodies will collide with one another with a thunderous crash, and the mountains will be crushed to dust and scattered. In such a situation, Allah tells the polytheists, by way of warning, that on that Day a cloud will appear splitting the sky, and on that Day the rows of angels will be sent down upon the disbelievers, just as they had demanded. After this, one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection is brought forward. In it, these misguided and wrongdoing people will be deeply ashamed. This scene is very long, so long that the spectators think it will go on forever. This wrongdoer is biting his own hands out of extreme remorse and regret.

His cries are so heart-rending, and their effect so long-lasting, that the assembly keeps growing longer, and the impressions become ever deeper. Their status is that of a trivial particle. Man's standing in this universe is established only when he connects himself with Allah and increases his weight through faith, thereby creating some value for himself. ﴿Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed greatly in insolence﴾ (25:21)

They are so intoxicated with themselves that they cannot weigh true values correctly. Now the habit of these people is that they perceive only their own selves. Their self is so great a thing in their eyes that in this universe they consider only their own selves to be significant: so great that even Allah, Glorified be His Majesty, should appear before it, so that they may see Him, confirm Him, and believe in Him.

Their condition will be that the punishment that cannot be averted will stand before them; they will see no way of escape from it, and this will be the day of punishment and recompense.

On the day this demand of theirs is fulfilled and the angels appear before them, they will see the angels. This was a phrase used to ward off evil and was said to enemies, invoking their destruction and seeking protection from their harm. This expression will escape their tongues in the Resurrection, just as in the world they used to utter it to seek refuge from evil. Today, how can they obtain the protection of God? Even if they seek the protection of God a million times today, it will benefit them nothing.

﴿And We will proceed to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ (25:23)

This process will be completed in an instant. All their deeds will be blown away like dust. Observe the manner of expression: our imagination sees it as a personal, embodied being coming and carrying off their deeds and scattering them like dust. This is the Qur'an's manner of embodiment and imagery. The meaning is that whatever they had gathered in the world in the form of righteous deeds will be reduced to dust. And this is because their deeds were not based on faith. Through faith alone does a person reach Allah. Faith gives righteous deeds a method, firmness and continuity, and these deeds have a purpose and a direction. They do not proceed from some momentary impulse, nor are they the running about of a person who knows no right path or direction, moving aimlessly here and there, or mere purposeless exertion. In Islam, no righteous deed has any value if it has no defined direction, no purpose, and no spirit, for such deeds bring no benefit at all.

The existence of man in this universe, his deeds, and the striving of his life are in fact connected with the reality of this universe. Man too is a part of the law of nature, and this entire universe is connected with the Divine Being. Man and all his activities are included in it. If man's striving, movement and exertion are cut off from this true light, they become purposeless. They are lost, and they have no weight or value before Allah. His deeds will have no reckoning, and they will have no value; rather, in the Islamic view, his existence is not even considered as such. He is merely wind and dust.

Faith brings man to the Lord. Thus, before the Lord of the worlds, his deeds also acquire weight, and a reckoning is kept for him in the account of this universe, and his deeds are displayed in the construction and progress of this universe. Since these polytheists have no faith, their deeds are rendered null and void. Yet the Qur'an has adopted a most concrete and sensory manner of expression.

Who are these insolent people, and what is their standing before Allah, who is Exalted, Mighty and Great? What standing do they have in His vast dominion and in this great universe? Their status is that of a trivial particle. Man's standing in this universe is established only when he connects himself with Allah and increases his weight through faith, thereby creating some value for himself. Therefore, before concluding this verse, Allah Himself tells us the cause of this insolence.

﴿Indeed, they have become arrogant within themselves and have transgressed greatly in insolence﴾ (25:21)

In their own estimation they are very great. Therefore they are engrossed in arrogance, and because of this arrogance they are involved in a very great rebellion. They are so intoxicated with themselves that they cannot weigh true values correctly. Now the habit of these people is that they perceive only their own selves. Their self is so great a thing in their eyes that in this universe they consider only their own selves to be significant: so great that even Allah, Glorified be His Majesty, should appear before it, so that they may see Him, confirm Him, and believe in Him.

Instead of answering their question, Allah, by way of mockery and derision, presents before them a picture of their misfortune and helplessness, and it is said that when on the Day of Resurrection they see the angels (seeing the angels was also one of their demands), then on that day evil will befall them. Their condition will be that the punishment that cannot be averted will stand before them; they will see no way of escape from it, and this will be the day of punishment and recompense.

﴿On the day they see the angels, there will be no good news that Day for the criminals; and they will say, "A forbidding forbidden."﴾ (25:22)

﴿And We will proceed to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ (25:23)

On the day this demand of theirs is fulfilled and the angels appear before them, they will see the angels. But on that day there will be no good tidings for them; rather, there will be news of punishment for them. Thus their demand will be fulfilled in a strange manner. On that day they will speak thus: ﴿A forbidding forbidden﴾ (25:22), meaning "God forbid!" This was a phrase used to ward off evil and was said to enemies, invoking their destruction and seeking protection from their harm. This expression will escape their tongues in the Resurrection, just as in the world they used to utter it to seek refuge from evil. Today, how can they obtain the protection of God? Even if they seek the protection of God a million times today, it will benefit them nothing.

﴿And We will proceed to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ (25:23)

This process will be completed in an instant. All their deeds will be blown away like dust. Observe the manner of expression: our imagination sees it as a personal, embodied being coming and carrying off their deeds and scattering them like dust. This is the Qur'an's manner of embodiment and imagery. The meaning is that whatever they had gathered in the world in the form of righteous deeds will be reduced to dust. And this is because their deeds were not based on faith. Through faith alone does a person reach Allah. Faith gives righteous deeds a method, firmness and continuity, and these deeds have a purpose and a direction. They do not proceed from some momentary impulse, nor are they the running about of a person who knows no right path or direction, moving aimlessly here and there, or mere purposeless exertion. In Islam, no righteous deed has any value if it has no defined direction, no purpose, and no spirit, for such deeds bring no benefit at all.

The existence of man in this universe, his deeds, and the striving of his life are in fact connected with the reality of this universe. Man too is a part of the law of nature, and this entire universe is connected with the Divine Being. Man and all his activities are included in it. His deeds will have no reckoning, and they will have no value; rather, in the Islamic view, his existence is not even considered as such. He is merely wind and dust.

Faith brings man to the Lord. Thus, before the Lord of the worlds, his deeds also acquire weight, and a reckoning is kept for him in the account of this universe, and his deeds are displayed in the construction and progress of this universe. Since these polytheists have no faith, their deeds are rendered null and void. Yet the Qur'an has adopted a most concrete and sensory manner of expression.

And let us also consider the condition of the believers, for comparison. These are the people of Paradise.

﴿The companions of Paradise will be, that Day, in a better dwelling place and a finer resting place at noon﴾ (25:24)

They will dwell in great comfort, joy and stability, in deep shade. The disbelievers used to make this demand of the Prophet ﷺ: that Allah should come before them in the shade of clouds, and that the angels should accompany him. All its heavens, its planets and stars will collide with one another. ﴿And the Day We set the mountains in motion, and you will see the earth laid bare﴾ (18:47)

The earth will be struck violently, the great celestial bodies will collide with one another with a thunderous crash, and the mountains will be crushed to dust and scattered. The seas will burst forth, either because of the upheavals of the earth's crust or because the particles of the seas will split apart, and through radiation the waters will catch fire. Bright stars will lose their light. The sky will split open and be torn into pieces. The stars and planets will collide with one another, be crushed, and scatter. All the vast distances of the heavens will vanish. The sun and moon will be joined together. At times the sky will be like black smoke, and at times like the flame of a fire. In short, it will be a dreadful hour, and in it a person will be overcome with terror.

In such a situation, Allah tells the polytheists, by way of warning, that on that Day a cloud will appear splitting the sky, and on that Day the rows of angels will be sent down upon the disbelievers, just as they had demanded. They did not make this demand in order to confirm Muhammad (ﷺ). These angels will come by the command of Allah, bringing the punishment of Allah.

﴿And that Day will be a hard day for the disbelievers﴾ (25:26). Because on that Day a severe punishment will be before them, it will be a terrifying day. These people demand the descent of the angels out of ignorance, whereas the angels come bringing punishment.

After this, one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection is brought forward. In it, these misguided and wrongdoing people will be deeply ashamed. This scene is very long, so long that the spectators think it will go on forever. This wrongdoer is biting his own hands out of extreme remorse and regret.

His cries are so heart-rending, and their effect so long-lasting, that the assembly keeps growing longer, and the impressions become ever deeper. Ubayy ibn Khalaf was also his friend, and he greatly shamed him, saying, "You have become irreligious." He replied, "By Allah, I have not accepted the religion of Muhammad." But he (Ubayy) said, "I will not accept your invitation until you utter the shahadah." Yet they (Muhammad and his companions) were in my house and did not eat my food. I felt very ashamed that he should not eat my food, so I recited the shahadah. Then Ubayy ibn Khalaf said, "By Allah, I will not be pleased with you unless you go and spit in his face, grasping his neck." The Prophet (ﷺ) was found prostrating in Dar al-Nadwah (the council house of Quraysh), and that wretched man did exactly this. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him that whenever he met him outside Makkah, he would cut off his head. This man was taken prisoner on the day of Badr, and the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) to cut off his neck.

﴿He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me﴾ (25:29). It was in fact Satan who was leading him astray, or was a helper of Satan.

﴿And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter﴾ (25:29). He brings the human being to the end of shame, and when the time of truth comes, Satan always runs away, especially in dreadful and anguishing scenes and occasions.

Thus the Qur'an shook the hearts of these people. It presented before them their end in the form of scenes that make one tremble, as though it were an event being witnessed before their eyes, even though those people are still upon this earth, denying Allah, rejecting with great contempt the prospect of appearing before Allah, and making demands that are foolish. Yet they are about to face an extremely terrifying situation there, and will be overwhelmed by utmost shame and remorse, but at that time remorse will be of no benefit.

Now the discourse turns from the scenes of the Day of Resurrection back to this world. The position they have taken regarding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is discussed. Now their objection is why the Qur'an was not revealed all at once. The present manner of the revelation of the Qur'an is objectionable to them. This question and answer also concludes with a scene of the Resurrection: just as their objection is reversed, so too they will be dragged upside down into Hell.

This lesson opens in the same manner as the previous lesson, and its theme proceeds in the same way; however, here the objections of the polytheists are directed at the Lord, the Exalted. Here they raise objections against Allah and prescribe for Him their own course of action. In other words, in this lesson they advance further in their arrogance: while objecting to the Messenger of Allah, they proceed to object against God Himself. This too is a way of consoling and encouraging the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, showing that they do not object to you alone, but their insolence extends even into the presence of Allah. ﴿Why are not the angels sent down to us, or why do we not see our Lord?﴾ (25:21)

An answer is given to this, and it is explained why the Qur'an was revealed continuously in parts. The Messenger is comforted, with the assurance that whenever they bring forth an argument, We also provide you with a new explanation and the best interpretation and clarification. After this, for the consideration of the Prophet and his opponents, a picture is also drawn of the time when some of the deniers were destroyed, and how these nations were annihilated. Just consider the ruins of the people of Lot; you pass by them day and night. The Qur'an seizes them sharply, because when they see those ruins day and night, their hearts are not affected in the least. All these matters have been brought in order that the objections they used to raise against the person of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ may be stated here in one place. ﴿And those who do not expect to meet Us say...﴾ (25:21) to ﴿...a forsaker for man﴾ (25:29)

In short, it will be a dreadful hour, and in it a person will be overcome with terror.

﴿So when vision is dazzled, and the moon darkens, and the sun and moon are joined﴾ (75:7–9)

﴿So when the stars are dimmed, and the sky is split open, and the mountains are blown away﴾ (77:8–10)

﴿And they ask you about the mountains. Say, "My Lord will blow them away as dust, and leave the earth a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or unevenness"﴾ (20:105–107)

﴿And you see the mountains, thinking them fixed, while they will pass away as clouds pass﴾ (27:88)

﴿And the Day We set the mountains in motion, and you will see the earth laid bare﴾ (18:47)

﴿On the Day the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens as well﴾ (14:48)

﴿On the Day when We will roll up the heaven like the rolling up of a scroll for writings﴾ (21:104). All these verses show that the end of this world of ours will be extremely terrifying. The earth will be struck violently, the great celestial bodies will collide with one another with a thunderous crash, and the mountains will be crushed to dust and scattered. The seas will burst forth, either because of the upheavals of the earth's crust or because the particles of the seas will split apart, and through radiation the waters will catch fire. Bright stars will lose their light. The sky will split open and be torn into pieces. The stars and planets will collide with one another, be crushed, and scatter. All the vast distances of the heavens will vanish. The sun and moon will be joined together. At times the sky will be like black smoke, and at times like the flame of a fire. In short, it will be a dreadful hour, and in it a person will be overcome with terror.

In such a situation, Allah tells the polytheists, by way of warning, that on that Day a cloud will appear splitting the sky, and on that Day the rows of angels will be sent down upon the disbelievers, just as they had demanded. They did not make this demand in order to confirm Muhammad (ﷺ). These angels will come by the command of Allah, bringing the punishment of Allah.

﴿And that Day will be a hard day for the disbelievers﴾ (25:26). Because on that Day a severe punishment will be before them, it will be a terrifying day. These people demand the descent of the angels out of ignorance, whereas the angels come bringing punishment.

After this, one of the scenes of the Day of Resurrection is brought forward. In it, these misguided and wrongdoing people will be deeply ashamed. This scene is very long, so long that the spectators think it will go on forever. This wrongdoer is biting his own hands out of extreme remorse and regret.

﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way. Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend. He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me. And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter."﴾ (25:27–29)

This person is expressing deep regret, and silence has fallen over his surroundings. This person keeps raising his regretful voice. His cries are so heart-rending, and their effect so long-lasting, that the assembly keeps growing longer, and the impressions become ever deeper. Even today, a reader of these verses is seized by deep regret, and those who witness the scene become sharers in the grief.

﴿And the Day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands﴾ (25:27). It is not only one hand that he will bite but both hands, now this one and now that one. Because of the intensity of his grief, he will vent his anger upon his own hands. The biting of the hands points to what the psychological state of the wrongdoer will be on that Day. His sorrow and anguish have been expressed through an embodied action and movement, meaning that he will be unable to bear the grief.

﴿He will say, "Oh, I wish I had taken with the Messenger a way"﴾ (25:27). That is, I wish I had followed the way of the Messenger of Allah, and had not separated myself from the Messenger, whose prophethood he had denied, on the grounds that this Messenger is a human being.

﴿Woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a friend﴾ (25:28). Here "so-and-so" is used generally, without naming anyone, so that all misguiding companions are included: every friend who leads friends toward error. However, the narrations state that the occasion of revelation of these verses was ʿUqbah ibn Abi Muʿayt. This man used to sit and rise very frequently with the Prophet (ﷺ). He invited the Prophet (ﷺ) to a feast, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said that he would not accept his invitation until he bore witness to two things. So he did so. Ubayy ibn Khalaf was also his friend, and he greatly shamed him, saying, "You have become irreligious." He replied, "By Allah, I have not accepted the religion of Muhammad." But he (Ubayy) said, "I will not accept your invitation until you utter the shahadah." Yet they (Muhammad and his companions) were in my house and did not eat my food. I felt very ashamed that he should not eat my food, so I recited the shahadah. Then Ubayy ibn Khalaf said, "By Allah, I will not be pleased with you unless you go and spit in his face, grasping his neck." The Prophet (ﷺ) was found prostrating in Dar al-Nadwah (the council house of Quraysh), and that wretched man did exactly this. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him that whenever he met him outside Makkah, he would cut off his head. This man was taken prisoner on the day of Badr, and the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) to cut off his neck.

﴿He led me away from the remembrance after it had come to me﴾ (25:29). It was in fact Satan who was leading him astray, or was a helper of Satan.

﴿And ever is Satan, to man, a deserter﴾ (25:29). He brings the human being to the end of shame, and when the time of truth comes, Satan always runs away, especially in dreadful and anguishing scenes and occasions.

Thus the Qur'an shook the hearts of these people. It presented before them their end in the form of scenes that make one tremble, as though it were an event being witnessed before their eyes, even though those people are still upon this earth, denying Allah, rejecting with great contempt the prospect of appearing before Allah, and making demands that are foolish. Yet they are about to face an extremely terrifying situation there, and will be overwhelmed by utmost shame and remorse, but at that time remorse will be of no benefit.

Now the discourse turns from the scenes of the Day of Resurrection back to this world. The position they have taken regarding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is discussed. Now their objection is why the Qur'an was not revealed all at once. The present manner of the revelation of the Qur'an is objectionable to them. This question and answer also concludes with a scene of the Resurrection: just as their objection is reversed, so too they will be dragged upside down into Hell.

(Waqal al-Rasul... wa-adalla sabeelan) "They abandoned this Qur'an which Allah had revealed to His servant, so that he might warn them and grant them insight. They forsook the Qur'an in such a way that they fled from even hearing it, out of fear that if they heard it, its irresistible influence would affect them, and they would be unable to reject its effects. Even if they did hear it, they gave no thought to its themes, so that they might attain the truth and follow its path. They abandoned it in such a way that they did not make it the constitution of their lives, although it had been revealed precisely so that they would make it their system of life."

(Waqal al-Rasul ya Rabbi... mahjooran) (25:30) "And the Messenger will say: 'O my Lord, my people had made this Qur'an an object of ridicule.'" Although the Lord knew that this had happened, this is a supplication and a turning to Allah in lament. Allah also knows, and Allah bears witness, that the Messenger ﷺ was not negligent in this matter; the fault lies with the people, who neither listened to the Qur'an nor reflected upon it.

Thus Allah consoles the Prophet ﷺ, that this is a general pattern of conduct experienced by all prophets. It is a continuing way (sunnah jariyah), and all the Messengers faced similar circumstances. All the prophets encountered situations in which their peoples ridiculed the Qur'an and their call, and turned people away from the path of Allah. Yet Allah's help remained with His Messengers, and Allah showed His Messengers such ways that they prevailed over their enemies.

(Wa kadhalika... wa nasiran) (25:31) "O Prophet, in this way We have made for every prophet enemies among the criminals, and your Lord suffices as a guide and helper for you." The wisdom of Allah leads to a good end. When criminals arise against an Islamic movement and become determined in opposition, this creates strength within the movement, and in this way the movement becomes serious. The very difference between a true call and a false call is that people rise up against the true call, and the bearers of the true call face difficulties. It is this struggle that distinguishes the call to truth from false calls. As a result of this struggle, the true followers separate out and stand firm, while the bearers of falsehood flee. Only those remain behind to support the call who are sincere and devoted, who are not slaves of interests, and for whom the Islamic call alone is their goal. They seek only the pleasure of Allah.

If the work of the Islamic call were easy, its response were applause, flowers were strewn on the path of the caller, and there were no enemy or critic, then everyone would become a bearer of the Islamic call. For there would be no opponent and no denier, and then there would be no difference between the call of truth and the call of falsehood, and disorder and turmoil would spread in the world. But Allah has raised up enemies and opponents against every true call, and has made struggle and confrontation necessary for the callers, and has made sacrifice in the path of truth and enduring hardships their way. Obviously, only one who is truthful strives in the way of Allah. Only one who is a true believer endures hardships and sacrifices. Those people who sacrifice their comfort and luxury for the call of truth, who renounce the pleasures of worldly life, and who even give up their lives in this path if the call demands that the time for laying down life has come, are the ones prepared for this great struggle. They are the ones who are firm and steadfast, who are true believers, who possess firm faith. They long more for the reward that is with Allah than for the reward that is with people. When such circumstances arise, the difference between the true call and the false call becomes clear. In such situations the ranks of the Islamic call are purified: the strong, the powerful and the steadfast are separated out, and the weak are set apart. Then the Islamic call advances with those people who have passed the test of steadfastness. It is they who become the trustees and leaders of this call and who bear its responsibility. These people reach that station by paying a heavy price. They fulfil the right of this call with truthfulness. With firm faith, experience and trials have shown them how to carry this call forward in the most difficult circumstances. Hardships and difficulties have made their whole strength sensitive, their source of strength and their store of power increase, and they hold aloft the banner of the call in the most difficult situations.

In this world it generally happens that in the struggle between the bearers of the Islamic call and their opponents, a great number of people remain neutral and watch as spectators. When this spectating population sees that the bearers of the Islamic call are making great sacrifices for their ideology and purpose, and are bearing immeasurable hardships, and are proceeding on their path with great steadfastness and single-mindedness, then these spectating common people begin to think why these people are making such sacrifices and bearing such hardships for the Islamic call. Obviously, these aims must be very beneficial and very precious, and they are sacrificing life, property, honour and dignity, perhaps because those aims are more precious than these things. Now these people try to understand the true value of the Islamic call. When the matter becomes clear to ordinary people, they then enter the Islamic call in crowds, and instead of watching the spectacle, they themselves become the spectacle.

This is the secret for which Allah created for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. These criminals strive to block the path of the Islamic call. Then the prophets and their followers, every bearer of truth, confront these criminals. They face difficulties, yet they keep walking on their path. For such people success is destined, and they are well aware that in the end they will reach that outcome. In the end they receive guidance and help.

(Wa kafa bi-rabbika hadiyan wa nasiran) (25:31) "And your Lord suffices as a guide and helper." The emergence of criminals on the path of the prophets is a natural matter, because the call of truth always appears at its appropriate and appointed time, when a particular society becomes corrupt, or all of humanity falls prey to corruption. The hearts and vision of people become corrupted, the order of the world deteriorates, and people's mutual relations are disturbed. Behind this corruption and deterioration stand criminals, who on the one hand create corruption and then on the other benefit from this corruption and disorder. They are of the same disposition and temperament as this corruption. Their desires are fulfilled within this corrupt society, and for the corruption and deterioration that exists within their own being, they seek a justification in society, saying that society is just like this. Therefore it is entirely natural that such people stand in the way of the prophets, and after the prophets' time they stand in the way of those who carry the prophets' message, because these criminals are in fact the defence of their own corrupted existence. For among insects there are some which cannot live at all in a pure, clean, fragrant and transparent environment; they die immediately, because they are accustomed to living in a filthy environment. Some worms die in clean water, because they can live only in dirty and rotten water. This is the condition of these criminals. Therefore it is a natural matter that they be enemies of the call of truth and be prepared to give their lives to oppose it, and it is equally natural that in the end the Islamic call should succeed, because the Islamic call moves upon the ever-advancing lights of life. In this way the Islamic call attains the exaltation which Allah has appointed for it.

(Wa kafa bi-rabbika hadiyan wa nasiran) (25:31) "And your Lord suffices as a guide and helper." Next, the objections of the disbelievers regarding the manner of the Qur'an's revelation are related, and they are refuted.

(Wa qal alladhina kafaru... tartilan) (25:32) "Those who disbelieve say: 'Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?'" ... "Yes, it was done this way so that We may firmly establish your heart by it, and We have arranged it in a distinct order and in separate portions."

The Qur'an was revealed precisely so that through it a community might be trained, a new society brought into being, and a new system established in that society. Training requires that a person be repeatedly admonished and continually influenced, and that this influence and impression continue through ongoing motion, since what is desired is the creation of revolution within human beings. Man is such a being that he cannot be trained in a single day and night, by simply handing him a book containing a new system with the complete features of a modern society. Rather, human beings are trained in such a way that they are changed gradually over a long period, and this change comes into them little by little. After each day's nourishment, the next day they are ready for more nourishment, and they receive the next day's sustenance with joy and accept it with great pleasure.

The Qur'an brought a complete system of life, and in training human beings it adopted a natural method. This method came from the One who created man, so the Qur'an was sent down in portions so that it might continually meet the real and living needs of the community of Muslims, because this community was being built gradually, advancing step by step according to its capacity and strength, in exact accordance with Allah's true method of training. Thus the Qur'an was sent down at once as a method of training and for the formation of a system of life. Therefore its gradual revelation was necessary. It was not merely a scholarly, cultural or literary book which, if composed in complete form, could be placed in people's hands so that they might read it and enjoy it without any need to act upon it. Rather, it came letter by letter, word by word, and command by command. Every verse came as an "order of the day." Muslims received commands and acted upon them, just as a soldier receives orders and carries them out. He takes the command, understands it and implements it. He himself is immersed in its condition, and he immerses society in it.

This is why the Qur'an was revealed in separate portions, so that it might firmly settle in the heart of the Messenger, and that before him it might first establish its steadfastness in him, and after each part, its next part would come, and it would continually be put into practice.

(Kadhalika li-nuthabbita bihi fuadak wa rattalnahu tartilan) (25:32) "Thus, so that We may firmly establish your heart by it, and We have arranged it in a distinct order." The meaning of tartil here is to reveal it in successive order according to Allah's wisdom, according to His knowledge and according to people's needs, and in accordance with the wisdom by which Allah knew how much capacity for accepting commands and guidance had come into being among the people.

Through its successive method of revelation, the Qur'an displayed miracles in the field of training these people. People continually received impressions from its revelation day by day, and their character was gradually formed. But because Muslims forgot the method of training of the Qur'an, and began to read it merely as knowledge and culture, and regarded it as a book which is only read, and did not consider it necessary to shape society according to it, nor to immerse themselves in its conditions, nor to establish a system of life according to it, then the Muslims gave up benefiting from this Qur'an, and the Qur'an stopped benefiting them, because the Muslims abandoned the very method of training which the All-Knowing, All-Aware had set down in the Qur'an, namely, that it be put into practice step by step.

The objections which the opponents of the Prophet ﷺ raised, the new objections they made, and the demands they put forward, the Qur'an, through its method of gradual revelation, answered each one satisfactorily.

(Wa la ya'tunaka... tafsira) (25:33) "And whenever they bring to you some strange argument, We have given you the correct answer at the proper time, and have explained the matter in the best manner." These people argued falsely, and Allah sent down truth in reply, which crushed falsehood. The purpose of the Qur'an was precisely that truth should become firmly established in the world. Success in mere debate was not the aim; rather, the aim was to give truth strength in the world, to make it clear, and to make it prevail.

Allah promises His Messenger ﷺ that He will help him in every kind of dispute between him and his people, because he is upon the truth, and Allah supports the truth with His help and destroys falsehood. How could their argument and debate stand against the conclusive proof established by Allah? For the Prophet ﷺ possessed the truth sent down by the Lord, which struck the head of falsehood like a projectile and crushed it.

This scene alone is sufficient to break their pride.
