Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 30–34 (part 2 of 2):

This matter now concludes with the theme of how they will be cast into Hell on the Day of Resurrection. Because they denied the truth, and in their disputation and opposition to Islam they used perverse logic, therefore on the Day of Resurrection too they will be dragged and thrown face-down.

﴿Those who will be gathered upon their faces into Hell, their position is very evil, and their way is extremely misguided.﴾ (25:34)

Look at their state on the Day of Gathering: they will be raised upon their faces, in a manner most humiliating. This is because in the world they used to turn away out of arrogance. This scene is presented before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that he may be consoled: these people trouble him now, but their end will be very evil. A depiction of this is placed before him. This scene alone is sufficient to break their pride. And these people, though they were affected and frightened by such scenes, nevertheless, through their obstinate argumentation, made that evil end binding upon themselves, and because of this enmity they wronged themselves.

Now the address turns back to the earlier nations who denied, and were destroyed.

(Waqal al-Rasul... wa-adalla sabeelan) "They abandoned this Qur'an which Allah had revealed to His servant, so that he might warn them and grant them insight. They forsook the Qur'an in such a way that they fled from even hearing it, out of fear that if they heard it, its irresistible influence would affect them, and they would be unable to reject its effects. Even if they did hear it, they gave no thought to its themes, so that they might attain the truth and follow its path. They abandoned it in such a way that they did not make it the constitution of their lives, although it had been revealed precisely so that they would make it their system of life."

(Waqal al-Rasul ya Rabbi... mahjooran) (25:30) "And the Messenger will say: 'O my Lord, my people had made this Qur'an an object of ridicule.'" Although the Lord knew that this had happened, this is a supplication and a turning to Allah in lament. Allah also knows, and Allah bears witness, that the Messenger ﷺ was not negligent in this matter; the fault lies with the people, who neither listened to the Qur'an nor reflected upon it.

Thus Allah consoles the Prophet ﷺ, that this is a general pattern of conduct experienced by all prophets. It is a continuing way (sunnah jariyah), and all the Messengers faced similar circumstances. All the prophets encountered situations in which their peoples ridiculed the Qur'an and their call, and turned people away from the path of Allah. Yet Allah's help remained with His Messengers, and Allah showed His Messengers such ways that they prevailed over their enemies.

(Wa kadhalika... wa nasiran) (25:31) "O Prophet, in this way We have made for every prophet enemies among the criminals, and your Lord suffices as a guide and helper for you." The wisdom of Allah leads to a good end. When criminals arise against an Islamic movement and become determined in opposition, this creates strength within the movement, and in this way the movement becomes serious. The very difference between a true call and a false call is that people rise up against the true call, and the bearers of the true call face difficulties. It is this struggle that distinguishes the call to truth from false calls. As a result of this struggle, the true followers separate out and stand firm, while the bearers of falsehood flee. Only those remain behind to support the call who are sincere and devoted, who are not slaves of interests, and for whom the Islamic call alone is their goal. They seek only the pleasure of Allah.

If the work of the Islamic call were easy, its response were applause, flowers were strewn on the path of the caller, and there were no enemy or critic, then everyone would become a bearer of the Islamic call. For there would be no opponent and no denier, and then there would be no difference between the call of truth and the call of falsehood, and disorder and turmoil would spread in the world. But Allah has raised up enemies and opponents against every true call, and has made struggle and confrontation necessary for the callers, and has made sacrifice in the path of truth and enduring hardships their way. Obviously, only one who is truthful strives in the way of Allah. Only one who is a true believer endures hardships and sacrifices. Those people who sacrifice their comfort and luxury for the call of truth, who renounce the pleasures of worldly life, and who even give up their lives in this path if the call demands that the time for laying down life has come, are the ones prepared for this great struggle. They are the ones who are firm and steadfast, who are true believers, who possess firm faith. They long more for the reward that is with Allah than for the reward that is with people. When such circumstances arise, the difference between the true call and the false call becomes clear. In such situations the ranks of the Islamic call are purified: the strong, the powerful and the steadfast are separated out, and the weak are set apart. Then the Islamic call advances with those people who have passed the test of steadfastness. It is they who become the trustees and leaders of this call and who bear its responsibility. These people reach that station by paying a heavy price. They fulfil the right of this call with truthfulness. With firm faith, experience and trials have shown them how to carry this call forward in the most difficult circumstances. Hardships and difficulties have made their whole strength sensitive, their source of strength and their store of power increase, and they hold aloft the banner of the call in the most difficult situations.

In this world it generally happens that in the struggle between the bearers of the Islamic call and their opponents, a great number of people remain neutral and watch as spectators. When this spectating population sees that the bearers of the Islamic call are making great sacrifices for their ideology and purpose, and are bearing immeasurable hardships, and are proceeding on their path with great steadfastness and single-mindedness, then these spectating common people begin to think why these people are making such sacrifices and bearing such hardships for the Islamic call. Obviously, these aims must be very beneficial and very precious, and they are sacrificing life, property, honour and dignity, perhaps because those aims are more precious than these things. Now these people try to understand the true value of the Islamic call. When the matter becomes clear to ordinary people, they then enter the Islamic call in crowds, and instead of watching the spectacle, they themselves become the spectacle.

This is the secret for which Allah created for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals. These criminals strive to block the path of the Islamic call. Then the prophets and their followers, every bearer of truth, confront these criminals. They face difficulties, yet they keep walking on their path. For such people success is destined, and they are well aware that in the end they will reach that outcome. In the end they receive guidance and help.

(Wa kafa bi-rabbika hadiyan wa nasiran) (25:31) "And your Lord suffices as a guide and helper." The emergence of criminals on the path of the prophets is a natural matter, because the call of truth always appears at its appropriate and appointed time, when a particular society becomes corrupt, or all of humanity falls prey to corruption. The hearts and vision of people become corrupted, the order of the world deteriorates, and people's mutual relations are disturbed. Behind this corruption and deterioration stand criminals, who on the one hand create corruption and then on the other benefit from this corruption and disorder. They are of the same disposition and temperament as this corruption. Their desires are fulfilled within this corrupt society, and for the corruption and deterioration that exists within their own being, they seek a justification in society, saying that society is just like this. Therefore it is entirely natural that such people stand in the way of the prophets, and after the prophets' time they stand in the way of those who carry the prophets' message, because these criminals are in fact the defence of their own corrupted existence. For among insects there are some which cannot live at all in a pure, clean, fragrant and transparent environment; they die immediately, because they are accustomed to living in a filthy environment. Some worms die in clean water, because they can live only in dirty and rotten water. This is the condition of these criminals. Therefore it is a natural matter that they be enemies of the call of truth and be prepared to give their lives to oppose it, and it is equally natural that in the end the Islamic call should succeed, because the Islamic call moves upon the ever-advancing lights of life. In this way the Islamic call attains the exaltation which Allah has appointed for it.

(Wa kafa bi-rabbika hadiyan wa nasiran) (25:31) "And your Lord suffices as a guide and helper." Next, the objections of the disbelievers regarding the manner of the Qur'an's revelation are related, and they are refuted.

(Wa qal alladhina kafaru... tartilan) (25:32) "Those who disbelieve say: 'Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?'" ... "Yes, it was done this way so that We may firmly establish your heart by it, and We have arranged it in a distinct order and in separate portions."

The Qur'an was revealed precisely so that through it a community might be trained, a new society brought into being, and a new system established in that society. Training requires that a person be repeatedly admonished and continually influenced, and that this influence and impression continue through ongoing motion, since what is desired is the creation of revolution within human beings. Man is such a being that he cannot be trained in a single day and night, by simply handing him a book containing a new system with the complete features of a modern society. Rather, human beings are trained in such a way that they are changed gradually over a long period, and this change comes into them little by little. After each day's nourishment, the next day they are ready for more nourishment, and they receive the next day's sustenance with joy and accept it with great pleasure.

The Qur'an brought a complete system of life, and in training human beings it adopted a natural method. This method came from the One who created man, so the Qur'an was sent down in portions so that it might continually meet the real and living needs of the community of Muslims, because this community was being built gradually, advancing step by step according to its capacity and strength, in exact accordance with Allah's true method of training. Thus the Qur'an was sent down at once as a method of training and for the formation of a system of life. Therefore its gradual revelation was necessary. It was not merely a scholarly, cultural or literary book which, if composed in complete form, could be placed in people's hands so that they might read it and enjoy it without any need to act upon it. Rather, it came letter by letter, word by word, and command by command. Every verse came as an "order of the day." Muslims received commands and acted upon them, just as a soldier receives orders and carries them out. He takes the command, understands it and implements it. He himself is immersed in its condition, and he immerses society in it.

This is why the Qur'an was revealed in separate portions, so that it might firmly settle in the heart of the Messenger, and that before him it might first establish its steadfastness in him, and after each part, its next part would come, and it would continually be put into practice.

(Kadhalika li-nuthabbita bihi fuadak wa rattalnahu tartilan) (25:32) "Thus, so that We may firmly establish your heart by it, and We have arranged it in a distinct order." The meaning of tartil here is to reveal it in successive order according to Allah's wisdom, according to His knowledge and according to people's needs, and in accordance with the wisdom by which Allah knew how much capacity for accepting commands and guidance had come into being among the people.

Through its successive method of revelation, the Qur'an displayed miracles in the field of training these people. People continually received impressions from its revelation day by day, and their character was gradually formed. But because Muslims forgot the method of training of the Qur'an, and began to read it merely as knowledge and culture, and regarded it as a book which is only read, and did not consider it necessary to shape society according to it, nor to immerse themselves in its conditions, nor to establish a system of life according to it, then the Muslims gave up benefiting from this Qur'an, and the Qur'an stopped benefiting them, because the Muslims abandoned the very method of training which the All-Knowing, All-Aware had set down in the Qur'an, namely, that it be put into practice step by step.

The objections which the opponents of the Prophet ﷺ raised, the new objections they made, and the demands they put forward, the Qur'an, through its method of gradual revelation, answered each one satisfactorily.

(Wa la ya'tunaka... tafsira) (25:33) "And whenever they bring to you some strange argument, We have given you the correct answer at the proper time, and have explained the matter in the best manner." These people argued falsely, and Allah sent down truth in reply, which crushed falsehood. The purpose of the Qur'an was precisely that truth should become firmly established in the world. Success in mere debate was not the aim; rather, the aim was to give truth strength in the world, to make it clear, and to make it prevail.

Allah promises His Messenger ﷺ that He will help him in every kind of dispute between him and his people, because he is upon the truth, and Allah supports the truth with His help and destroys falsehood. How could their argument and debate stand against the conclusive proof established by Allah? For the Prophet ﷺ possessed the truth sent down by the Lord, which struck the head of falsehood like a projectile and crushed it.

The hearts and vision of people become corrupted, the order of the world deteriorates, and people's mutual relations are disturbed. Behind this corruption and deterioration stand criminals, who on the one hand create corruption and then on the other benefit from this corruption and disorder. They are of the same disposition and temperament as this corruption. Their desires are fulfilled within this corrupt society, and for the corruption and deterioration that exists within their own being, they seek a justification in society, saying that society is just like this. Therefore it is entirely natural that such people stand in the way of the prophets, and after the prophets' time they stand in the way of those who carry the prophets' message, because these criminals are in fact the defence of their own corrupted existence. For among insects there are some which cannot live at all in a pure, clean, fragrant and transparent environment; they die immediately, because they are accustomed to living in a filthy environment. Some worms die in clean water, because they can live only in dirty and rotten water. This is the condition of these criminals. Therefore it is a natural matter that they be enemies of the call of truth and be prepared to give their lives to oppose it, and it is equally natural that in the end the Islamic call should succeed, because the Islamic call moves upon the ever-advancing lights of life. In this way the Islamic call attains the exaltation which Allah has appointed for it.

(Wa kafa bi-rabbika hadiyan wa nasiran) (25:31) "And your Lord suffices as a guide and helper." Next, the objections of the disbelievers regarding the manner of the Qur'an's revelation are related, and they are refuted.

(Wa qal alladhina kafaru... tartilan) (25:32) "Those who disbelieve say: 'Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?'" ... "Yes, it was done this way so that We may firmly establish your heart by it, and We have arranged it in a distinct order and in separate portions."

The Qur'an was revealed precisely so that through it a community might be trained, a new society brought into being, and a new system established in that society. Training requires that a person be repeatedly admonished and continually influenced, and that this influence and impression continue through ongoing motion, since what is desired is the creation of revolution within human beings. Man is such a being that he cannot be trained in a single day and night, by simply handing him a book containing a new system with the complete features of a modern society. Rather, human beings are trained in such a way that they are changed gradually over a long period, and this change comes into them little by little. After each day's nourishment, the next day they are ready for more nourishment, and they receive the next day's sustenance with joy and accept it with great pleasure.

The Qur'an brought a complete system of life, and in training human beings it adopted a natural method. This method came from the One who created man, so the Qur'an was sent down in portions so that it might continually meet the real and living needs of the community of Muslims, because this community was being built gradually, advancing step by step according to its capacity and strength, in exact accordance with Allah's true method of training. Thus the Qur'an was sent down at once as a method of training and for the formation of a system of life. Therefore its gradual revelation was necessary. It was not merely a scholarly, cultural or literary book which, if composed in complete form, could be placed in people's hands so that they might read it and enjoy it without any need to act upon it. Rather, it came letter by letter, word by word, and command by command. Every verse came as an "order of the day." Muslims received commands and acted upon them, just as a soldier receives orders and carries them out. He takes the command, understands it and implements it. He himself is immersed in its condition, and he immerses society in it.

This is why the Qur'an was revealed in separate portions, so that it might firmly settle in the heart of the Messenger, and that before him it might first establish its steadfastness in him, and after each part, its next part would come, and it would continually be put into practice.

(Kadhalika li-nuthabbita bihi fuadak wa rattalnahu tartilan) (25:32) "Thus, so that We may firmly establish your heart by it, and We have arranged it in a distinct order." The meaning of tartil here is to reveal it in successive order according to Allah's wisdom, according to His knowledge and according to people's needs, and in accordance with the wisdom by which Allah knew how much capacity for accepting commands and guidance had come into being among the people.

Through its successive method of revelation, the Qur'an displayed miracles in the field of training these people. People continually received impressions from its revelation day by day, and their character was gradually formed. But because Muslims forgot the method of training of the Qur'an, and began to read it merely as knowledge and culture, and regarded it as a book which is only read, and did not consider it necessary to shape society according to it, nor to immerse themselves in its conditions, nor to establish a system of life according to it, then the Muslims gave up benefiting from this Qur'an, and the Qur'an stopped benefiting them, because the Muslims abandoned the very method of training which the All-Knowing, All-Aware had set down in the Qur'an, namely, that it be put into practice step by step.

The objections which the opponents of the Prophet ﷺ raised, the new objections they made, and the demands they put forward, the Qur'an, through its method of gradual revelation, answered each one satisfactorily.

(Wa la ya'tunaka... tafsira) (25:33) "And whenever they bring to you some strange argument, We have given you the correct answer at the proper time, and have explained the matter in the best manner." These people argued falsely, and Allah sent down truth in reply, which crushed falsehood. The purpose of the Qur'an was precisely that truth should become firmly established in the world. Success in mere debate was not the aim; rather, the aim was to give truth strength in the world, to make it clear, and to make it prevail.

Allah promises His Messenger ﷺ that He will help him in every kind of dispute between him and his people, because he is upon the truth, and Allah supports the truth with His help and destroys falsehood. How could their argument and debate stand against the conclusive proof established by Allah? For the Prophet ﷺ possessed the truth sent down by the Lord, which struck the head of falsehood like a projectile and crushed it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 30–34 (part 2 of 2):

This matter now concludes with the theme of how they will be cast into Hell on the Day of Resurrection. Because they denied the truth, and in their disputation and opposition to Islam they used perverse logic, therefore on the Day of Resurrection too they will be dragged and thrown face-down.

﴿Those who will be gathered upon their faces into Hell, their position is very evil, and their way is extremely misguided.﴾ (25:34)

Look at their state on the Day of Gathering: they will be raised upon their faces, in a manner most humiliating. This is because in the world they used to turn away out of arrogance. This scene is presented before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so that he may be consoled: these people trouble him now, but their end will be very evil. A depiction of this is placed before him. This scene alone is sufficient to break their pride. And these people, though they were affected and frightened by such scenes, nevertheless, through their obstinate argumentation, made that evil end binding upon themselves, and because of this enmity they wronged themselves.

Now the address turns back to the earlier nations who denied, and were destroyed.

(Part 1 of 2 — Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran, on Surah al-Furqan, verses 35–44)

(Wa laqad atainā… wa wazīrā) (35–40)

These are brief examples which show the end of those who denied the truth. Moses (peace be upon him) was given the Book, and his brother Aaron was made his minister and helper in prophethood, and they were sent to the people who denied the signs of Allah.

﴿Al-qawm alladhīna kadhdhabū bi-āyātinā﴾ (25:36): These were Pharaoh and his chiefs, who denied the signs of Allah. The meaning is that these people were denying the signs of Allah even before Moses and Aaron were granted the office of prophethood, because the signs of Allah are permanent. They exist in the universe and within the self (anfus). The task of the messengers is only to draw people's attention to them. Before the second verse has even ended, the end is announced with great severity.

﴿Fa-dammarnāhum tadmīrā﴾ (25:36): "So We utterly destroyed them."

Then comes the case of the people of Noah:

﴿Kadhdhabū al-rusul aghraqnāhum﴾ (25:37): "They denied the messengers, so We drowned them."

The people of Noah had denied only one messenger, Noah (peace be upon him). But the reality is that the belief which Noah presented to them was the belief of all the prophets. When they denied Noah, it was as if they had denied all the messengers.

﴿Wa ja'alnāhum lil-nāsi āyah﴾ (25:37): "And We made them a sign for mankind." Because the miracle of the flood can never be forgotten. Whoever reflects on the event of the flood will gain a lesson.

﴿Wa a'tadnā lil-ẓālimīna ʿadhāban alīmā﴾ (25:37): "And for the wrongdoers We have prepared a painful punishment." This punishment is ever-present; no preparation is needed for it. The word "zālimīn" (wrongdoers) is used in place of a pronoun so that it becomes their permanent title, and so that it is also made clear that this punishment is given to them because of their wrongdoing. Then [the examples include] ʿĀd, Thamūd, and the Companions of the Rass (those whose well had no walls built around it). It is said that these people lived in a village in Yamamah and killed their prophet. Ibn Jarīr, however, has said that they are the Companions of the Ukhdūd (the trench), who burned the believers, which is mentioned in Surah al-Burūj. And others who came in later eras, all of them Allah destroyed and made a sign of warning. They did not reflect upon the call of the prophets and could not escape destruction.

All these examples—the people of Moses, Noah, ʿĀd, Thamūd, the Companions of the Rass, the intervening generations, and the people (of Lot) upon whom a rain of stones fell—all reached one path and one end, and Allah made them all an object of lesson.

﴿Wa kullan tabbarnā tatbīrā﴾ (25:39): "And We destroyed each one utterly." Because they denied the prophets, and nations that deny the prophets are struck by ruin and destruction. Here Allah casts a swift glance over the tragic end of all these nations, and this rapid account concludes with the story of Lot's people, whose settlements on the main road near Sodom and Zoar are clearly visible to passers-by. Allah destroyed that people through an upheaval of the earth; stones were rained down upon them, and thus they were completely annihilated. It is astonishing that, despite seeing and hearing all this, these people still take no lesson from the end of the deniers. They do not fear the Day of Resurrection in their hearts; they do not fear standing before Allah. This is only because their hearts have become like stone and have been transformed. For this reason, they have adopted malice, enmity, arrogance and mockery towards the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they raise all kinds of objections against the Qur'an.

After this brief survey of the nations who denied, the discourse now turns to the mocking manner of these people. Previously they had also committed similar insolence regarding Allah, and had said why the Qur'an was being revealed in its present form. It is astonishing that, despite seeing and hearing all this, these people still take no lesson from the end of the deniers. They do not fear the Day of Resurrection in their hearts; they do not fear standing before Allah. This is only because their hearts have become stone and have been transformed. For this reason, they have adopted malice, enmity, arrogance and

(Wa idhā ra'awka… sabīlā) (41–44)

"When they see you, they make you a subject of mockery [saying]: 'Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger? He would have led us astray from our gods had we not remained steadfast in their worship.' Soon they will know, when they see the punishment, who has strayed furthest from the path. Have you considered the one who has taken his own desire as his god? Can you take responsibility for guiding such a person? Do you think that most of them hear and understand? They are only like cattle, rather even further astray."

The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) was known among his people. Before his prophethood, he was a highly respected man among them. He was a prominent member of the Banu Hashim, who were the leading clan of the Quraysh. Because of his character he held a great status and position, and before his prophethood he was known as al-Ṣādiq (the truthful) and al-Amīn (the trustworthy). When, during the rebuilding of the Ka'bah, the Quraysh disputed over who should place the Black Stone, all agreed that he should set it in place. And when he called them to al-Ṣafā and asked them whether, if he said that an army was coming at them from beyond that mountain, they would accept his word, they all said: "Yes, you are not one to tell lies in our eyes."

But after the Prophet (ﷺ) presented the Qur'anic call following his commission, it was these same people who mocked Muhammad (ﷺ).

﴿A-hādhā alladhī baʿatha Allāhu rasūlā﴾ (25:41): "Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?" They said this sentence as mockery. Was it that they wished to mock the person of the Prophet (ﷺ), or was there something in the Qur'an that could be mocked? No; neither of these was the case. Rather, they said this as part of a deliberate plan by the chiefs of the Quraysh. Through it they wished to defame the great personality of the Prophet (ﷺ), and thereby to control the powerful effects of the Qur'an. They adopted this strategy to confront the new call, because the status and rank they held in the former society was threatened, and some of their economic interests were tied to the former system of ignorance (jahiliyyah). Their position and economic standing were due to the ideological superstitions that dominated Arab society, and the Qur'an was uprooting those meaningless superstitions.

These people used to hold great assemblies to counter the new call. In these gatherings they made such false propaganda and fabricated character-assassination decisions, even though they knew well that they were speaking falsely. Ibn Ishaq relates that once some men of the Quraysh were sitting with al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. He was an elderly and wise man. The season of Hajj was approaching, and he said to the Quraysh: "The season of Hajj is coming, and delegations from all over the Arab world will come to Makkah. They have heard about your man, so it is appropriate that you unite your opinion about him, lest you say different things and contradict one another." They said: "Abu ʿAbd al-Shams, you tell us, and form an opinion, and we will all say the same thing." He said: "First you tell me what you will say, so that I may see what you say." They said: "We will say that he is a soothsayer (kāhin)." He said: "By God, he is not a soothsayer. We have seen soothsayers; he does not murmur like them, nor speak in rhymed prose like them." They said: "Then we will say he is possessed (majnūn)." He said: "He is not possessed. We have seen and known the possessed; there is no choking of the throat like the possessed, no agitation and no whispering." They said: "Then we will say he is a poet." He said: "He is not a poet. We all know the types and meters of poetry: rajaz, hazaj, qarīḍ, maqbūḍ and mabsūṭ." They said: "Then we will say he is a sorcerer." He said: "He is not a sorcerer. We have seen sorcerers and their sorcery; he neither blows like them nor ties knots." They said: "Abu ʿAbd al-Shams, you tell us what we should say." He said: "By God, his speech is very sweet; its root is firm and its branches are like fresh blossoms. Whatever you say of it, people will know it is a false statement. Yet the most fitting thing you can say is that he is a sorcerer, and his speech is so enchanting that it separates a man from his father, his brother, his wife and his family." So they left him with this decision. When the season of Hajj came, they sat on the roads, and whoever passed by them they warned and told about Muhammad (ﷺ).

This is an example of their deep conspiracy and plotting against the Messenger (ﷺ), and they carried it out knowing that the Messenger (ﷺ) was truthful. Therefore, what they said—"Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"—was not said as mockery, but as a deliberate conspiracy and mere character-assassination, even though their own consciences bore witness that they regarded him as upon the truth. By saying these things they lowered the Prophet's (ﷺ) standing in the eyes of the common people, so that the honour and rank they held in the former system would remain, and the material benefits they used to receive would continue to flow to them. The conduct of the Quraysh towards the Messenger (ﷺ) is the same conduct that self-interested people adopt towards the call to truth in every time and place.

Outwardly they spread propaganda in a mocking manner and assassinated his character, but their own words revealed how deeply they were disturbed by the call of the Messenger (ﷺ). They also made this comment about the decisive arguments of the Qur'an:

﴿In kāda la-yuḍillunā ʿan ālihatinā law lā an ṣabarnā ʿalayhā﴾ (25:42): "He would have led us astray from our gods had we not remained steadfast in their worship." In truth, there was a kind of earthquake in their mental world. They were close to abandoning their gods, but they clung firmly to their gods with steadfastness, and they protected their religion and the interests linked with it. Had they not done so, that is, had they not opposed and shown patience and perseverance, they too would have abandoned their gods. It is astonishing that, because of their obstinacy and their interests, these people called guidance misguidance. This was indeed their misguidance: they were calling wisdom madness. Yet they could not conceal the tremor that the call of Muhammad (ﷺ) had caused in their halls. Although, out of extreme obstinacy and insistence, they found fault with the person of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, Allah warns them that very soon they will reach their end.

﴿Wa sawfa ya'lamūna ḥīna yarawna al-ʿadhāba man aḍallu sabīlā﴾ (25:42): "Soon they will know, when they see the punishment, who has strayed furthest from the path." They will clearly come to know that the call which Muhammad (ﷺ) brought was guidance, and that what they held to was misguidance. But when the time passes, knowledge is of no further use. At that time they will see the punishment, whether it be the punishment of this world—as they tasted on the day of Badr—or the punishment of the Hereafter, which they will see, know and taste on the Day of Reckoning.

Now the discourse turns again to Muhammad (ﷺ). He is consoled regarding their obstinacy, stubbornness and mockery: you have not fallen short in conveying the message. You have set out the arguments in full, and it was not right that their response should be what it has been. The fault is theirs alone. In truth, they have taken their own carnal desires as their god, and they are not inclined to heed any sincere appeal or clear proof. If people do not accept, what can the Messenger (ﷺ) do?

﴿A-ra'ayta man ittakhadha ilāhahu hawāhu afa-anta takūnu ʿalayhi wakīlā﴾ (25:43): "Have you considered the one who has taken his own desire as his god? Can you then be responsible for him?" This is a strange manner of expression. It reveals their peculiar psychological state: a person abandons all established standards, all accepted reasoning and all settled values, and begins to worship only his own desire, his own preference and his own stubbornness. He pays no heed to any argument, proof, logic or serious matter. He simply worships his desire as a god.

Allah, glory be to Him, calls His servant with great gentleness, affection, intimacy and deep closeness: "Have you considered?" "Do you know?" This is a portrait of a person before whom it is futile to present any sound argument. He does not know proof, truth or reflection; these things have no value in his eyes. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told, by way of consolation, that such a person is not fit for guidance. Consequently, you cannot be held responsible for guiding such a person, nor can you be his guardian, and such people cannot reach guidance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 25, verses 35–44 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Then would you be a guardian over him?﴾ (25:43) "Can you take responsibility for guiding such a person to the right path?" Here the true status and real rank of those who have made their desires their deity and their god is also made clear: they are very base people. They are merely slaves of their own desires and interests. They do not bow before proof and truth; rather, they prostrate before their desires and interests. Indeed, they are given an even lower rank: having fallen from the station of humanity, they have entered the station of pure animality, and even below that.

﴿Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are only like livestock; rather, they are even further astray in the way.﴾ (25:44) "Do you think that most of them hear and understand? They are like animals, rather even worse off." Here Allah has adopted a very careful manner of speech. He says "most of them" (aktharihum), not all of them, meaning that the majority are like this, because a small number of the people of Makkah had already embraced Islam at the very beginning, or most of them were reflecting on it. Rather, the majority were those who, out of mere passion for their desires and for their interests, would not accept. Arguments fell upon their ears and their intellect acknowledged them, yet they still stubbornly insisted. They were, as it were, mere animals. The very difference between a human being and an animal is that a human reflects, and then a human adopts good conduct in accordance with his reflection. With insight and deliberate intention he embraces realities; he speaks with proof and argument, and he listens. And if a human abandons these distinguishing qualities, he becomes worse than beasts, because beasts make use of the awareness Allah has given them, whereas humans do not make use of the reason and wisdom that has been given to them. Animals fulfil their assigned duties properly, but humans do not. Animals benefit from their consciousness, while these people do not exercise their reflection.

﴿They are not but like livestock... and further astray in the way.﴾ (25:44) This is the answer to their mockery: that is, you are not even human beings; you are worse than animals. Therefore, you mock the Master of both worlds, Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Thus this passage concludes with a response to their scoffing.

They said: "Abu ʿAbd al-Shams, you tell us, and form an opinion, and we will all say the same thing." He said: "First you tell me what you will say, so that I may see what you say." They said: "We will say that he is a soothsayer (kāhin)." He said: "By God, he is not a soothsayer. We have seen soothsayers; he does not murmur like them, nor speak in rhymed prose like them." They said: "Then we will say he is possessed (majnūn)." He said: "He is not possessed. We have seen and known the possessed; there is no choking of the throat like the possessed, no agitation and no whispering." They said: "Then we will say he is a poet." He said: "He is not a poet. We all know the types and meters of poetry: rajaz, hazaj, qarīḍ, maqbūḍ and mabsūṭ." They said: "Then we will say he is a sorcerer." He said: "He is not a sorcerer. We have seen sorcerers and their sorcery; he neither blows like them nor ties knots." They said: "Abu ʿAbd al-Shams, you tell us what we should say." He said: "By God, his speech is very sweet; its root is firm and its branches are like fresh blossoms. Whatever you say of it, people will know it is a false statement. Yet the most fitting thing you can say is that he is a sorcerer, and his speech is so enchanting that it separates a man from his father, his brother, his wife and his family." So they left him with this decision. When the season of Hajj came, they sat on the roads, and whoever passed by them they warned and told about Muhammad (ﷺ).

This is an example of their deep conspiracy and plotting against the Messenger (ﷺ), and they carried it out knowing that the Messenger (ﷺ) was truthful. Therefore, what they said—"Is this the one whom Allah has sent as a messenger?"—was not said as mockery, but as a deliberate conspiracy and mere character-assassination, even though their own consciences bore witness that they regarded him as upon the truth. By saying these things they lowered the Prophet's (ﷺ) standing in the eyes of the common people, so that the honour and rank they held in the former system would remain, and the material benefits they used to receive would continue to flow to them. The conduct of the Quraysh towards the Messenger (ﷺ) is the same conduct that self-interested people adopt towards the call to truth in every time and place.

Outwardly they spread propaganda in a mocking manner and assassinated his character, but their own words revealed how deeply they were disturbed by the call of the Messenger (ﷺ). They also made this comment about the decisive arguments of the Qur'an:

﴿In kāda la-yuḍillunā ʿan ālihatinā law lā an ṣabarnā ʿalayhā﴾ (25:42): "He would have led us astray from our gods had we not remained steadfast in their worship." In truth, there was a kind of earthquake in their mental world. They were close to abandoning their gods, but they clung firmly to their gods with steadfastness, and they protected their religion and the interests linked with it. Had they not done so, that is, had they not opposed and shown patience and perseverance, they too would have abandoned their gods. It is astonishing that, because of their obstinacy and their interests, these people called guidance misguidance. This was indeed their misguidance: they were calling wisdom madness. Yet they could not conceal the tremor that the call of Muhammad (ﷺ) had caused in their halls. Although, out of extreme obstinacy and insistence, they found fault with the person of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the Qur'an, Allah warns them that very soon they will reach their end.

﴿Wa sawfa ya'lamūna ḥīna yarawna al-ʿadhāba man aḍallu sabīlā﴾ (25:42): "Soon they will know, when they see the punishment, who has strayed furthest from the path." They will clearly come to know that the call which Muhammad (ﷺ) brought was guidance, and that what they held to was misguidance. But when the time passes, knowledge is of no further use. At that time they will see the punishment, whether it be the punishment of this world—as they tasted on the day of Badr—or the punishment of the Hereafter, which they will see, know and taste on the Day of Reckoning.

Now the discourse turns again to Muhammad (ﷺ). He is consoled regarding their obstinacy, stubbornness and mockery: you have not fallen short in conveying the message. You have set out the arguments in full, and it was not right that their response should be what it has been. The fault is theirs alone. In truth, they have taken their own carnal desires as their god, and they are not inclined to heed any sincere appeal or clear proof. If people do not accept, what can the Messenger (ﷺ) do?

﴿A-ra'ayta man ittakhadha ilāhahu hawāhu afa-anta takūnu ʿalayhi wakīlā﴾ (25:43): "Have you considered the one who has taken his own desire as his god? Can you then be responsible for him?" This is a strange manner of expression. It reveals their peculiar psychological state: a person abandons all established standards, all accepted reasoning and all settled values, and begins to worship only his own desire, his own preference and his own stubbornness. He pays no heed to any argument, proof, logic or serious matter. He simply worships his desire as a god.

Allah, glory be to Him, calls His servant with great gentleness, affection, intimacy and deep closeness: "Have you considered?" "Do you know?" This is a portrait of a person before whom it is futile to present any sound argument. He does not know proof, truth or reflection; these things have no value in his eyes. Therefore the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) is told, by way of consolation, that such a person is not fit for guidance. Consequently, you cannot be held responsible for guiding such a person, nor can you be his guardian, and such people cannot reach guidance.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 25, verses 35–44 (part 2 of 2):

﴿Then would you be a guardian over him?﴾ (25:43) "Can you take responsibility for guiding such a person to the right path?" Here the true status and real rank of those who have made their desires their deity and their god is also made clear: they are very base people. They are merely slaves of their own desires and interests. They do not bow before proof and truth; rather, they prostrate before their desires and interests. Indeed, they are given an even lower rank: having fallen from the station of humanity, they have entered the station of pure animality, and even below that.

﴿Or do you think that most of them hear or understand? They are only like livestock; rather, they are even further astray in the way.﴾ (25:44) "Do you think that most of them hear and understand? They are like animals, rather even worse off." Here Allah has adopted a very careful manner of speech. He says "most of them" (aktharihum), not all of them, meaning that the majority are like this, because a small number of the people of Makkah had already embraced Islam at the very beginning, or most of them were reflecting on it. Rather, the majority were those who, out of mere passion for their desires and for their interests, would not accept. Arguments fell upon their ears and their intellect acknowledged them, yet they still stubbornly insisted. They were, as it were, mere animals. The very difference between a human being and an animal is that a human reflects, and then a human adopts good conduct in accordance with his reflection. With insight and deliberate intention he embraces realities; he speaks with proof and argument, and he listens. And if a human abandons these distinguishing qualities, he becomes worse than beasts, because beasts make use of the awareness Allah has given them, whereas humans do not make use of the reason and wisdom that has been given to them. Animals fulfil their assigned duties properly, but humans do not. Animals benefit from their consciousness, while these people do not exercise their reflection.

﴿They are not but like livestock... and further astray in the way.﴾ (25:44) This is the answer to their mockery: that is, you are not even human beings; you are worse than animals. Therefore, you mock the Master of both worlds, Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). Thus this passage concludes with a response to their scoffing.

Lesson No. 159 — At a Glance

In this lesson, leaving aside the objections of the polytheists and the debates the Prophet ﷺ had with them, we are taken on a tour of the sights and scenes of this universe. The heart and feelings of the Prophet ﷺ are turned towards this universe. To clear away the dust of discouragement caused by the frivolous objections of the polytheists, this connection with the scenes of the universe and this attention towards them is sufficient. This journey through the vastness of the universe is a broad field for the tranquillity of your heart and the expansion of your breast, and in comparison to it, the petty plots of the plotters and the aimless enmities of the enemies appear extremely insignificant.

The Holy Qur'an always turns the minds and hearts of human beings towards reflecting upon the observable realities of this universe. A connection is established between human thought, human reflection and observations of divine power. It awakens the faculties of human consciousness and perception and prepares them to see its observations and scenes with a completely fresh sensation, to hear the call of the observable signs of divine power and the wonders of nature, and to respond to that call. The Qur'an commands man to travel through this universe and to take from it the scattered proofs of divine power and the signs of nature. For this universe is in reality an open book, and on its pages the craftsmanship and artistry of the Creator (Sani' al-Kainat) are awaiting our contemplation. The Holy Qur'an commands man to seek out the traces of the Hand of divine power. He should keep his eye seeing, his sensation sharp and his ears open, and through these faculties of perception search for subjects of reflection and contemplation. In this way he attains connection with Allah (ittisal ba-Llah), that is, he attains recognition of Allah's Being through the craftsmanship of Allah.

When a person lives in this universe with an open heart and open eyes, with his soul and his feelings awake, and with his thought and his reasoning well-ordered, he rises above the ordinary attachments of the world. His outlook on life becomes elevated, and his sensitivity becomes very keen. Then he begins to think that compared to this limited world, the horizons of the universe are very vast. Then, that whatever exists in this universe exists as the result of one single will. All these things are bound within one single law of life. Then, in their movement, all these things are directed towards one single Creator. And man himself is one of the creatures of this universe, and he too is bound to the Hand of divine power, and his whole environment is held in the grip of the Hand of divine power. Whatever he sees and whatever he touches are the craftsmanship of divine power.

From this conception, a combined state of consciousness of piety (taqwa), consciousness of love and consciousness of trust emerges upon the screen of human feeling. Through this the soul of man is filled, his world is filled with meaning, and he attains a special inner purification, tranquillity, and intimacy and love. Thus, with this spirit, this understanding and this conception, man walks upon this earth, and in the end he is united with Allah. In this way, human life becomes a most pleasant recreational journey. He becomes lost in an exhibition and a fair of Allah's craftsmanship, and at every moment he is at a spread of divine blessings, arranged in various kinds, within this beautiful universe of Allah.

The lesson begins with a depiction of the shade. The Hand of divine power makes the shade longer and then gradually contracts it. This process of expansion and contraction takes place very gently, delicately and imperceptibly. Then we rush in the darkness of night towards our resting places. The whole universe is overtaken by calm and silence. Then we enter the day, and the struggle of life begins in a most orderly manner. Then the winds of mercy blow, bring clouds and send down rain. Then we are in the sea, where sweet water and salt water are mixed side by side, and between the two there is a barrier which is the craftsmanship of the Hand of divine power. These two seas and these two waters do not mingle with each other. Then, from ordinary waters, we come to the vessel of life of man. It is a drop of semen. Suddenly it takes on the form of a living human being. Then in another scene we see that the creation of the whole heavens and earth is in six days. Within the heavens and the earth there are constellations (buruj). There are the shining lamp and the illuminating moon. Then night and day follow one another, and ages pass.

Within this journey through the universe, our hearts come alive, and our thought becomes lost in the craftsmanship of the Creator who orders all things, and the sights of divine power and its governance are renewed in the heart of man. Then man reflects how foolish the polytheists are, that they associate partners with that Lord and worship such things as can neither benefit them nor harm them. Man reflects how ignorant these people are about the Lord, the Exalted, and how boldly they act against the Being of Allah, and how they display disbelief and denial. In the presence of these proofs, signs and wonders of manifest evidence within this universe, the conduct of the polytheists appears extremely strange. These scenes of the universe and these samples of Allah's creation are sufficient and healing for human guidance.

Come, let us take a brief tour of these wonders of the Hand of divine power, every aspect of which is sufficient to unite us with Allah, and a single valley of which is sufficient for the whole of our lives.

(Alam tara ... qabdan yasira) (25: 45–46)

The very idea of a spacious and gentle shade is refreshing for a dejected and weary person. In such a shade a person feels himself extremely tranquil. He feels as though a most merciful and generous hand of compassion is touching his soul and body, and that a most soothing dressing is being applied to the wounds of life. The environment of nature provides a hand of compassion to weary hearts. Did Allah desire that His servant, having been subjected to all kinds of accusations and mockery and having had his heart hurt, should be given this environment of natural compassion? He should be taken out for a while from this agonizing environment of struggle and given an environment of natural tranquillity, and the heart of the Prophet ﷺ, wounded in this mighty battle, should be given tranquillity. Remember that this is the Meccan period, and a long time has passed in which you have been confronting the obstinacy, denial, arrogance and enmity and deceit of the Quraysh polytheists. Your companions are few, the polytheists are spread out on every side, and by Allah's command you and the believers are not permitted to respond to this torment, mockery and aggression.

The truth is that in such difficult circumstances, whatever portion of the Qur'an was revealed upon your heart acted as a most soothing salve. It was in reality a broad and deep shade for a weary traveller, and within the hot wind of disbelief, denial, enmity and partisanship it was a cool and pleasant shelter. The shade, especially in a scorching desert, within the hot atmosphere of this surah's spirit, its theme, its subject matter and its disputation, provides peace, tranquillity and a refuge.

The Holy Qur'an depicts this shade in such a way that the Hand of divine power lengthens it. It gradually lengthens in an imperceptible manner. Then it is folded up with the utmost gentleness and imperceptibly.

Alam tara ila Rabbika kayfa madda'z-zill (25:45) "Have you not seen how your Lord spreads out the shade?"

Thumma qabadnahu ilayna qabdan yasira (25:46) "Then We gradually draw it in towards Us."

What is shade? When a body comes between the rays of the sun and an object, it creates a slight kind of darkness. As the earth moves in front of the sun, this shade also keeps moving. Its form and its shape keep changing. Its shape and appearance are determined by the rays of the sun, through light and heat, due to which it contracts and expands. Because of this, a person attains joy and freshness, a delicate and clear wakefulness arises within his soul, and the human self can clearly observe the subtle craftsmanship of the Hand of divine power. When this scene of the sun and the shade comes to its close, this shade keeps lengthening more and more. When it reaches the final limit of its length, this shade disappears with the setting of the sun. Where has it gone? Is this not the Hand of divine power which has folded and gathered it up? A comprehensive shade spreads, and within it the darkness of night gradually begins to appear. This is the craftsmanship of the Hand of divine power. Man is immersed within these signs and indications of divine power. Around him the evidences of divine power are spread out, but his dull intellect does not perceive these signs.

Wa law sha'a laja'alahu sakinan (25:45) "Had He willed, He would have made it stationary."

But Allah did not will that. For the arrangement of this universe has been ordained in precisely this way. The requirement of this order is that we keep seeing this shade daily in such a way that its ebb and flow continues just as it is. If even a slight change were made in it, and this shade were made stationary, the entire signs of this universe would change. If the earth were stationary in one place, this shade too would be stationary, and its ebb and flow would come to an end. If the movement of the earth were slow, the signs of this shade too would be slow in motion, and if the movement of the earth were swift, the ebb and flow of the shades too would become swift. It is a determined motion of the earth which bestows upon the shades those manifestations which we see, and produces those effects which are beneficial to us and whose properties we understand well.

This rotation of the earth and the movement of the shades and their ebb and flow we see day and night and pass through in heedlessness. Allah the Exalted turns us afresh towards this. This is a particular method of the Qur'an's style of expression: it revives a dead impression within the human conscience. It awakens receptivity within us and connects us with our environment. It awakens our feelings and sharpens our consciousness, so that we may reflect upon the depth of these observations and clear signs. Thus our hearts become accustomed to reflection upon this universe, because this universe is very great and wondrous.

This scene of the shade ends at nightfall. When the shades lengthen, the night spreads. Behind the veil of the night humanity attains rest and tranquillity, and then comes the day, in which people enter into the struggle of life.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verse 47:

وھو الذی ……نشوراً (47)

The night covers all things and all living creatures. It appears as though everything has wrapped itself in the cloak of the night. People hide themselves behind the veil of the night. Thus the night becomes a garment for them. There is complete tranquility in the night. The movement of everything comes to a halt. Human beings, animals and even birds fall asleep. Furthermore, after sleep, the awareness of this world that a person has while awake does not remain. For this reason, it (sleep) is described as subat (rest), that is, a tranquility like death. Then the morning appears and movement begins again upon the earth. In this way, it is as though after death everything is raised to life again. For this reason it is described as nushur (resurrection). Thus, in this earthly cycle of twenty-four hours, a human being presents a brief yet complete example of life and death. And since Allah created the earth and the heavens, this cycle of the earth has continued upon its axis. There has not been even a second's difference in it. This earth continues carrying human beings along, yet human beings are heedless and do not think about this movement of the earth at all, whereas the majesty of Allah that sustains this earth cannot be heedless for a single moment, and Allah does not feel drowsiness.

Now let us look at the second scene: the winds that come bearing the good news of rain.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 48–49:

﴿And He it is who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down pure water from the sky, that We may give life thereby to a dead land and give drink to many of the cattle and people We have created.﴾

Every life in this world rests upon water: either it is rainwater, or rivers and streams are harnessed through canals to give water to the surface of the earth. Then, of those waters which enter into the belly of the earth, some emerge in the form of springs, or are drawn out in the form of wells. Yet this too is rainwater. But for those people whose irrigation depends solely upon rain, they can well understand the mercy of Allah that falls in the form of rain. Day and night they are hopeful of rain, because their life rests upon rain. They wait for those winds which carry the clouds laden with mercy. When these winds come, they are glad tidings for them. They realise that these rains are the mercy of Allah. When Allah has opened the hearts of such people to Islam, they feel very deeply this mercy of Allah.

Here the concept of purity (taharah) and purifier (tahur) is highlighted along with water. ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾ (25:38). Its purpose is that within it lies the secret of life: ﴿That We may give life thereby to a dead land and give drink to many of the cattle and people We have created﴾ (25:39). Here a reflection of purity falls upon life, because it is Allah's will that human life be pure and clean. Moreover, this rain also cleanses and washes the face of the earth, and from this pure water life is produced, and the life of humans, animals and all living things is sustained.

A comment on the revelation of the Qur'an alongside the sending down of water: the purpose of the descent of water is the cleansing of the face of the earth, while the purpose of the descent of the Qur'an is the cleansing and perfection of the human soul. It is surprising that people wait for the descent of rain to strengthen the bond of body and soul, yet for spiritual purification they do not welcome the descent of the Qur'an, and they do not give one another glad tidings of it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 48–49:

﴿And He it is who sends the winds as glad tidings before His mercy, and We send down pure water from the sky, that We may give life thereby to a dead land and give drink to many of the cattle and people We have created.﴾

Every life in this world rests upon water: either it is rainwater, or rivers and streams are harnessed through canals to give water to the surface of the earth. Then, of those waters which enter into the belly of the earth, some emerge in the form of springs, or are drawn out in the form of wells. Yet this too is rainwater. But for those people whose irrigation depends solely upon rain, they can well understand the mercy of Allah that falls in the form of rain. Day and night they are hopeful of rain, because their life rests upon rain. They wait for those winds which carry the clouds laden with mercy. When these winds come, they are glad tidings for them. They realise that these rains are the mercy of Allah. When Allah has opened the hearts of such people to Islam, they feel very deeply this mercy of Allah.

Here the concept of purity (taharah) and purifier (tahur) is highlighted along with water. ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾ (25:38). Its purpose is that within it lies the secret of life: ﴿That We may give life thereby to a dead land and give drink to many of the cattle and people We have created﴾ (25:39). Here a reflection of purity falls upon life, because it is Allah's will that human life be pure and clean. Moreover, this rain also cleanses and washes the face of the earth, and from this pure water life is produced, and the life of humans, animals and all living things is sustained.

A comment on the revelation of the Qur'an alongside the sending down of water: the purpose of the descent of water is the cleansing of the face of the earth, while the purpose of the descent of the Qur'an is the cleansing and perfection of the human soul. It is surprising that people wait for the descent of rain to strengthen the bond of body and soul, yet for spiritual purification they do not welcome the descent of the Qur'an, and they do not give one another glad tidings of it.

And We have repeatedly explained this Qur'an to them, so that they may take heed. It comes in different surahs, through varied modes of expression and in many separate portions, and through it We addressed their awareness and their power of perception. We addressed their spirits and their minds, and tried to make it penetrate their souls in every way. For this purpose We used every means of communication, so that these people might accept admonition. Here only a reminder is needed. The awareness of truth and reality already exists within their own souls and their own nature, but they have suppressed this awareness of truth because they have made their own desires their god. Therefore, their attitude has now become this:

﴿But most people refuse to accept anything except disbelief and ingratitude.﴾ The responsibility of the Messenger ﷺ is a heavy one. He has to set right the whole of humanity, whereas the majority of people have become slaves of their personal desires, and despite the proofs of faith being scattered everywhere, they have decided to disbelieve.

﴿And if We had willed, We could have raised a warner in every town.﴾ In that case the burden would have been divided and the responsibilities would have been lessened. But Allah sent one single servant for the guidance of the entire universe. He (ﷺ) is the Seal of the Messengers, and he has been charged with warning all people and all towns and directing them towards Allah's final message. Thus Allah willed that all of humanity should unite upon this final message, so that people would not fall into dispute by listening to the words of different messengers. After this, He gave the Qur'an to the Prophet of the last age, so that he might strive for the guidance of the people.

﴿So do not obey the disbelievers, and strive against them with it, a great striving.﴾ O Prophet, do not by any means obey the disbelievers, and with this Qur'an struggle against them with a tremendous struggle. The Qur'an possesses great power and a firm grip, a deep impact, and such attraction that no listener can resist it. Its allure shakes hearts, and an upheaval takes place within the human spirit and consciousness. People employ every stratagem to nullify the effects of the Holy Qur'an, but they do not succeed.

The chiefs of Quraysh used to tell the common people:

"Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise where it is being recited, perhaps in this way you may prevail." Through this statement of theirs, the bewilderment of Quraysh and their leaders is revealed. They were greatly disturbed by the impact of the Holy Qur'an. They saw that their followers, morning and evening, were enchanted by the Holy Qur'an. Whenever the Messenger of Allah, Muhammad (ﷺ), recited one verse, two verses, or two surahs, people's hearts were drawn towards him and their minds became captivated.

Did the leaders of Quraysh, who instructed their followers in this way, themselves remain safe from the influence of the Qur'an? Had they not felt the overwhelming influence of the Holy Qur'an themselves, they would not have said such a thing, nor would they have spread such fear within their ranks. From this instruction of theirs it is well understood what the power of the Qur'an's influence was.

Ibn Ishaq narrates from Muhammad ibn Muslim ibn Shihab al-Zuhri that it reached him that Abu Sufyan, Abu Jahl ibn Hisham, and Akhnas ibn Shariq ibn Amr ibn Wahb al-Thaqafi, an ally of Banu Zuhrah, went out one night to listen to the words of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to pray at night in his house. Each of them sat down in his own particular place and kept listening to the Qur'an, and each did not know about the others. They kept listening until late into the night. When dawn broke, they began to return. On the way they met one another. They reproached each other and said to one another: "Do not repeat this act. If your foolish ones were to see you, you would plant doubt in their hearts." Then they departed. When the second night came, each of them again came and sat in his place, and they again kept listening to the word of Allah throughout the night. When the dawn appeared, they dispersed again. On the way they once more saw one another, and once again they said to each other what they had said the previous night. After that they went to their own homes. When the third night came, all three again reached their respective places and listened throughout the night. When dawn appeared, they dispersed again, but on the way they met once more. Now they said to one another: "Now we must make a firm pledge that we will not do this again." Following this covenant, they separated.

On the next morning, Akhnas ibn Shariq took his staff and went out. He first found Abu Sufyan at his home. He said to him: "Abu Hanzalah, tell me, what is your opinion about the words you heard from Muhammad (ﷺ)?" Abu Sufyan replied: "Abu Tha'labah, by Allah, I have heard some things from him which I understand and grasp their meaning, and I have heard some things whose meaning I do not understand, nor do I know what their purpose is." Akhnas said: "My opinion is also the same as the one you have sworn to." From there, this man came out and went to Abu Jahl. He entered his house and said: "Abu al-Hakam, tell me, what is your opinion about what you heard from Muhammad (ﷺ)?" Abu Jahl said: "What have I heard? The matter is this: there has always been a dispute between us and Banu Abd Manaf over honour and nobility. They fed people, so we also laid out tables in competition. They gave gifts to people, so we also gave gifts of loads of camels. They gave generously, so we also gave generously. Until we went side by side, like two competing horses running alongside each other. Now they have said that a Prophet has come to them, to whom revelation comes from heaven. How can we produce a prophet to match them? By Allah, we will never believe in him, and we will never affirm him." Upon this, Akhnas ibn Shariq left him and went away.

This was the state of the effect of the Holy Qur'an. These people were trying to counter its effects. They made firm pledges to one another that they would not listen again, otherwise the leadership would be in danger. If the common people came to know that we are enjoying the word of Allah, they would fall upon them, for its effect upon them is like magic.

In truth, the Holy Qur'an was expounding extremely simple and natural realities. This truth would penetrate the heart like an arrow. When human hearts and minds reached this genuine source, the surge of that fountainhead was extraordinary. Fountains of effects would burst forth. In it were scenes of the Resurrection, instructive narratives, observations of this universe, lessons from the stories of destroyed nations and the scenes of their ruins, the Qur'an's clear concepts and meanings, parables, events, and proofs and signs, and hearts would tremble at them. Sometimes merely reciting a single surah would produce a tremor within a human personality, and such human souls, which were as firm as a rock, would be conquered by it one after another. Even if a mighty army had sought to conquer such souls, it could not have done so.

Therefore, it is no surprise that Allah commands His Prophet (ﷺ) not to obey the disbelievers, and that his steps should not waver with regard to the call to Islam, and that with this Qur'an he should strive with a great striving against the disbelievers. For he possesses the power of the Holy Qur'an, before which the most powerful of men cannot stand. No argument can prevail against it, and no force can prevail against it.
