Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verse 53:

After this, the address turns to the scenes of this universe. Thus, the scenes of the winds, the scenes of pure and clean water, and the scenes of the sweet and salty waters in the seas, and of the natural barrier that lies between them, are described.

﴿And it is He who has let loose the two seas: this one sweet and palatable, and that one salty and bitter; and He has placed between them a barrier and a forbidding partition.﴾ (25:53)

That is, the One who has set the seas flowing, one sweet and the other salty and bitter, and although they are placed side by side, they do not mix with each other. Between them, God has placed a barrier. He has made their very natures such that they cannot mingle. Above the bitter seas there are streams of sweet water. A stream of sweet water flows over the surface of the sea; the reverse seldom happens, that is, a stream of bitter water does not flow over a sweet sea. Because of this precise arrangement, the bitter water of the sea does not rise over the clean and sweet water. Yet the bitter sea is very vast and deep, while the sweet stream is small, but by this sweet stream the life of humans, animals and plants is sustained. This flow of sweet and bitter waters does not occur by mere chance; rather, the Creator of the universe brought them into being in this manner at the time of creation, and the Creator had certain purposes in view. God has placed in the laws of nature that the bitter waters shall not block the path of these streams, nor shall these seas rise up over the land. Even in the tides of the sea, the sweet water and the bitter sea remain separate from one another, although at the time of the tide the water of the sea rises very high.

The author of the book "Science Invites to Faith" says: "The moon is two hundred and forty thousand miles away from us. The tide that occurs twice gives us a subtle sense of the moon's existence. Because of the tide, at certain places the surface of the sea rises sixty feet, and indeed the upper surface of the earth also bulges outward by several inches twice a day because of the moon's pull. Yet all things appear to us so orderly that we are not even aware of this force, which has raised this great sea several feet and, having found the surface of the earth which appears to us very firm, has made it several inches taller."

"The planet Mars has a moon of its own. It is a small moon, and it is about six thousand miles from Mars. If our moon were fifty thousand miles away from us, in comparison with the great distance at which it is now, the process of the tide would be so intense that the land beneath the sea would, being subjected twice a day to this tidal process, uproot all its mountains from their places. By continuing in this way, all dry land in the world would disappear and there would be a perpetual great upheaval on the earth. Moreover, as a result of the tidal process, fierce storms would continually arise in the air. And if we assume that this tide of ours has washed away the dry land, then we must assume that now the water has risen over the entire earth to a depth of one and a half miles. In that case, if there were any abode for life, it would be in the depths of the sea, and even this is only a possibility of the existence of life."

But this universe has been made by an all-wise Creator in such a way that, even within the sea, sweet and salty water cannot encroach upon one another. And within their natural disposition and their structure He has placed the fact that they do not mix with each other. This is the work of the wise Maker who has organized this universe and set it in motion according to a specific law of nature.

Now the focus of address turns from the seas and rivers of water to the water of life. Consider the drop of semen from which a human being is created.

﴿And it is He who has created from water a human being and made him [a line of] lineage and in-law relationship; and your Lord is ever Competent.﴾ (25:54)

From this same water, embryos are created. If the embryos are male, they become lineage (nasab), and if they are female, they become in-laws (sihr). The female is called sihr only because the place of kinship is the woman (that is, kinship comes into being through the woman). Compared with the creatures produced from rainwater from the sky, this human creation is most wondrous. For within a single drop of male fluid there are thousands of cells, and one of them unites with the small ovum present in the womb, and from this there comes into being that intricate creature called the human being. Among all living creations and beings, this creature is the most wondrous.

These ova and these cells are alike, yet in a wondrous manner they become male or female. Human beings have not yet discovered the secret of this either. Even today our knowledge has not reached the point of knowing what the causes of becoming male or female are, because no cell has been observed among the thousands of cells that distinguishes it, and no characteristics have been discovered in it by which one could know that it will be male or female. Nor has any characteristic been discovered within the woman's ovum such that, if certain characteristics are present, a male will be produced, and if certain others are present, a female will be produced.

﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾ (25:53). This is the power of Allah, some aspects of which have been unveiled in the modern age, revealing further wonders.

If a person keeps investigating the water from which human beings are created, his head will spin. When he sees that these germs found in that water, which are extremely small and fine, carry within them the most complete characteristics of each kind. Indeed, the traits of the parents and of their close family members are fully present within them, and these characteristics pass on by themselves to male and female embryos in the manner in which the hand of divine power has pre-planned them, in terms of creation, in terms of inclination, and in terms of way of life. Read for a little while the book "This Human Being Does Not Stand Alone." Its author writes about the hereditary genes found within these extremely tiny particles:

"Every cell, whether male or female, consists of chromosomes and genes. The chromosome is the basic unit of organic matter, and it performs the function of transmitting genes, while genes are hereditary characteristics. This chromosome is a kernel-like body within which all the genes exist. It is the genes that are the factors which determine the future of this human being coming into existence. Cytoplasm is that strange chemical compound which covers both of them. This cytoplasm is protoplasmic matter which sits over the kernel of the cell. These genes are so fine and so comprehensive that within them are the individual characteristics of all humans, their psychological conditions, their colour, and the characteristics of their sex. These are so fine that if the genes of all the people of the world were gathered into one place, the volume would be equal to a 'thimble.'"

"These extremely fine genes visible under a microscope are in fact the key to all humans, animals and plants, and they control them. The thimble, within which the genes of several billion individuals fit, is certainly a small space, but it is an established fact and there is no doubt about it."

When an embryo, passing through its various stages of change and transformation, takes on the likeness of one of the sexes from the semen, there lies hidden within it the story of a long history. This story has been recorded through the observation of genes and the particles of cytoplasm.

"It has been proven among scientists that genes are the smallest particles which can be seen through a microscope, and they are present within the cells of all living creatures; within them is the picture of that creature, its structure, and all its characteristics. For example, within the cell of a plant, its roots, its stem, its leaves, all its flowers and all its fruits are all present. The form, skin, hair and feathers of every animal are included, and human beings are included as well."

I think that to know just this much about the wonders of life is sufficient, to understand how much capacity the Creator of the universe has bestowed.

﴿And your Lord is ever Competent﴾ (25:53)

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 25, verse 55:

In this atmosphere of creation, and within creation the decree of God, and before this scene in which water descends from the heavens, and through it, and then from the water of human semen, what is produced, and what characteristics are placed in which genes, such that from a single cell a man is formed with all his hereditary qualities, and then from a similar single cell a woman is born with all her qualities. Even seeing the diverse manifestations of the power of such an Almighty Creator, those people who worship other than Allah are extremely strange. Sound human nature recoils from the idea that any rational person could do such a thing. Therefore, this matter is taken up here.

﴿And they worship, besides Allah, that which neither benefits them nor harms them, and the disbeliever is ever a helper against his Lord.﴾ (25:55)

"That the disbeliever is a helper against his Lord, against every rebel." That is, all disbelievers, including the polytheists of Makkah, are engaged in fighting by joining the front against their Lord, even though Allah created them and all other disbelievers. How can they join a front against Allah and wage war against Him? How can a human being, this weak creature, wage war against the Creator of the universe, or how can he oppose Allah in any way? The meaning is that these disbelievers are fighting against the religion of Allah. They are at war against the way of life that He has given. However, the manner of expression has been chosen so that this war and opposition of the disbelievers appears extremely abhorrent, as if to say: look, so-and-so is fighting against his master, lord and creator.

And when they deny the Messenger of Allah and his prophethood, they are in effect denying Allah. Therefore, their war is also against Allah. In this way Allah reassures His servant and eases his burden of distress, removes the weight upon his heart, and makes the Messenger (ﷺ) aware that he should simply fulfill his duty of conveying the message of prophethood and not care about the enmity and hostility that the disbelievers display in this regard. Let him place his trust in Allah; Allah Himself will deal with these disbelievers. Indeed, they are the enemies of Allah, and Allah is well aware of the crimes of His servants.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 56–59:

Wa ma arsalnaka ... bihi khabira (59)

In this way, the limits of the duty of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ are defined: that you are only a bringer of good news and a warner of evil consequences. And in Makkah you were not commanded to fight the people, because in Makkah there was complete freedom to propagate the religion. But later, when the Muslims migrated to Madinah, Allah commanded fighting (qital). In Makkah Allah did not command it, and in Madinah He commanded fighting. Its true wisdom is known only to Allah. What we understand is this: in that period, those people were being trained on whom this way of life depended, in whose hearts this belief had firmly settled, and whose lives were the interpreter of this belief. This belief had settled into their conduct and their way of life, so that after this training, the people would become the backbone of any society over which an Islamic government would be established later. And a second reason may also be this: if fighting had begun in Makkah, then because of those bloody enmities, the Quraysh would have been permanently deprived of this belief, and a permanent gulf would have arisen between them and Islam. Whereas, in the wisdom and decree of Allah, it was destined that after the Hijrah, and then after the Conquest of Makkah, all of the Quraysh would enter Islam, and then those among them who were to rise would serve as the foundation for the spread of Islam throughout the world in later eras.

However, despite the commencement of jihad in Madinah, the true nature and essence of prophethood remained that the Messenger's work was "warning and giving good news." As for fighting, it has been permitted so that if any obstacle has been placed in the path of the Islamic call and giving warning and good news in any region of the world, it may be removed. In Islam, war is undertaken solely so that if there is any obstacle in the path of the call and propagation, it may be removed. Therefore, this verse, "And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good news and a warner" (25:56), applies to the circumstances of Madinah just as it is correct for Makkah.

Qul ma as'alukum 'alayhi min ajrin illa man shaa'a an yattakhidha ila rabbihi sabilan (25:57–58)

"Say: I do not ask you for any wage for this work; my wage is only that whoever wishes should take the path to his Lord." Because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ has no personal benefit in people accepting Islam. Neither does he seek fees from anyone, nor does the Messenger seek the income of offerings, vows and sacrifices. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ had not fixed any fee for entry into Islam. A person would merely utter a few words and believe them sincerely in his heart. This was Islam, because in Islam there is no priest who would take a fee for making people holy, nor is there any broker between Allah and the people who takes commission for his brokerage. In Islam there is no ritual for entry, no secret, and no special ceremony to be performed at the time of entry. From this it becomes clear how simple, natural and innate a religion Islam is. It is simply a belief that enters the heart. Between the human heart and the belief of Islam there is no formal intermediary: no priest, no spiritual guide or saint. The reward of the Messenger is only this: that the true religion enters a person's heart and a servant draws near to his true Lord.

Illa man shaa'a an yattakhidha ila rabbihi sabilan (25:57) "This is the reward: that whoever wishes should take the path to his Lord." Only this reward is the Messenger's. The pure heart and pure consciousness of the Messenger are content only with this reward: that a lost servant finds the way to his Lord. The Lord is pleased, and he walks on the way of his Lord and turns towards his Master throughout his whole life.

Wa tawakkal 'ala ... bihamdihi (25:58) "And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die, and glorify Him with His praise." Every creature other than Allah is mortal, because all this creation is moving day and night towards death. The One who remains is Allah alone; He is the Living who never dies. To rely upon a living being who will one day die, after a long life or a short one, is to rely upon a being who will one day fall, a shade that will one day decline. Reliance should be placed only upon the One who is living and will never die. Glorify Him with His praise and declare His purity. Praise and thanks are also to be offered to Allah alone, who is the true Bestower and the true Giver. O Prophet, do not concern yourself with those disbelievers upon whom warning and good news have no effect. Allah knows well about those people.

Wa kafa bihi bidhunubi 'ibadihi khabira (25:58) "Sufficient is His being aware of the sins of His servants." Allah is thoroughly aware of the circumstances of His servants, so He can give reward and punishment, and He has the power to do so, for He created the heavens and the earth and He is established firmly upon the Throne of sovereignty.

Alladhi khalaqa ... khabira (25:59) "He who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days, then established Himself upon the Throne. The Most Merciful. Ask about Him one who is aware." The days in which Allah created the heavens and the earth were different from our earthly days, because these days began after the formation of the solar system. That is, after the creation of the heavens and the earth, when Allah set the earth's orbit around the sun and the earth began to rotate on its axis, our days began as a result. Allah's creation occurs only by the word "Be," meaning that when Allah commands, everything comes to be. As for these six days, their reality and measure is known only to Allah. They will be very long days, and during them the heavens and the earth passed through various stages and transformations before coming into their present form. As for how Allah established Himself upon the Throne, it means only that Allah has sovereignty and dominion over this universe. Here the word "thumma" (then) does not denote chronological sequence, i.e., that first the creation occurred and afterwards the establishment upon the Throne. That is not the case. Here "thumma" is used in the sense of exaltation and elevated rank.

After this exalted majesty and mighty sovereignty of Allah, He is also Ar-Rahman. Ask whomever you wish about Him; when you ask, you will be asking One who is most thoroughly aware, who knows everything in the heavens and the earth.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verse 60:

واذا قیل ……نفوراً (60)

When these self-deluded people are called to worship the Most Merciful (al-Rahman), they ask, with utmost contempt and irritation, "What is al-Rahman?"

This is the most wretched and repugnant picture of disbelief and rebellion. It shows how bold and insolent these people had become toward the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In their opposition to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they were prepared to insult their Lord as well. They adopted this manner of speech even about Allah. Therefore, if they used harsh words about the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), it was not surprising from them. They denied one of the names of Allah in this way, and they gave the impression that they did not know al-Rahman at all, as if it was none of their concern.

وما الرحمٰن (25:60) "What is al-Rahman?" They would say this with complete audacity, claiming: "We do not know al-Rahman except as the one who is in Yamamah." They were pointing to Musailamah al-Kadhdhab (the Liar).

The response to their audacity is given in this manner: Allah is the blessed Being whose greatness, whose blessings, and whose majesty are witnessed by this entire universe. Just reflect upon a single manifestation of this vast universe.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 61–62:

Blessed is He who... (until) ...grateful (64)

The correct explanation of al-buruj (the constellations/towers) is that it refers to the orbits of the planets: those great astronomical orbits which are a manifestation of far-reaching effects and far-reaching workings. This greatest of the cosmic phenomena has been presented by Allah, the Exalted, in answer to the disbelievers' remark, "What is al-Rahman?" They are told: consider what you think al-Rahman is. Just try to comprehend this creation of al-Rahman and your head would spin. It is truly great. Within these buruj the sun also moves in its course; it is a lamp, for the earth is illuminated by its light, and by its light the moon too is luminous, whose light is gentle and pleasant.

Here the continuous succession of night and day is presented for human observation, because these are two phenomena and miracles that are constantly being repeated before us, and if a person reflects upon these alone, they are sufficient and healing for his guidance.

"For whoever desires to remember or desires to be grateful" (25:62): for the person who wishes to take a lesson or ought to be grateful. If this system of the alternation of night and day were not as it is, the survival of human life on this earth would not be possible. There would be no humans, no animals, and no plants. Even if the present duration of day and night, twenty-four hours, were lengthened, life would still become difficult to sustain.

In the book "Science Calls to Faith" it is written:

"This earth, that is, the planet Earth, revolves on its axis in twenty-four hours. Its speed is one thousand miles per hour. If it is supposed that it were to rotate at only one hundred miles per hour, then our days and nights would become ten times longer. In that condition, the part upon which the sun was shining would be burnt to a crisp by the sun, and whatever was on the earth during the night would be frozen solid."

Therefore blessed is that Being who created everything in due proportion. And blessed is that Being who placed the buruj in the heavens and placed a lamp and a luminous moon, and who made the night and the day succeed one another. In this is a lesson for the one who wishes to take heed or to give thanks.

"This earth, that is, the planet Earth, revolves on its axis in twenty-four hours. Its speed is one thousand miles per hour. If it is supposed that it were to rotate at only one hundred miles per hour, then our days and nights would become ten times longer. In that condition, the part upon which the sun was shining would be burnt to a crisp by the sun, and whatever was on the earth during the night would be frozen solid."

Therefore blessed is that Being who created everything in due proportion. And blessed is that Being who placed the buruj in the heavens and placed a lamp and a luminous moon, and who made the night and the day succeed one another. In this is a lesson for the one who wishes to take heed or to give thanks.

Lesson No. 160 – At a Glance

In this fourth lesson of the surah, the servants of the Most Merciful (ʿIbād al-Raḥmān) are shown with their distinguishing qualities, and the basic features of their character are described. Though they are the essence of humanity, the salt of the earth, and the ultimate goal of the entire caravan of the Messengers, the struggle between truth and falsehood, and human history, they are, as it were, the ripened fruit of the garden of humanity. They are the outcome of the long struggle of the people of guidance against disbelief, ingratitude, aversion and disobedience.

At the end of the previous lesson, the disbelievers refused to recognise the Most Merciful and feigned ignorance. Here it is said: you do not acknowledge the Most Merciful, yet look at the servants of the Most Merciful. These are the people who truly recognise the Most Merciful. They are worthy of the title that they may be called the servants of the Most Merciful. Consider their persons, observe their character, their lives are an open book; read it. They stand before you as living examples in practice. This is the kind of community and the kind of society that Islam wishes to bring into being. These are the souls that Islam wishes to produce through its method of training, and these are the people whom Allah values on this earth. Allah's favours descend upon such people. Had these people not existed, Allah would have had no concern for all of mankind. It is indeed the blessing of the prayers of such people that sustains this universe.

﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility, and when the ignorant address them, they say, "Peace."﴾ (25:63)

Those in whose gait there is no affectation or pretence. There is no arrogance or pride in them, nor any laziness or sluggishness. That is, their walk is dignified. Here "walk" refers to their overall personality, which includes the moderation of intellect and character of a person, due to which moderation comes into all of a person's qualities and all of their actions, and because of these balanced qualities, a moderation and dignity come into the conduct of that person as well. Such a person is content and dignified, and in every kind of circumstance there is a composure within them.

The phrase ﴿يَمْشُونَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ﴾ (25:63) does not mean that they walk on the earth like dejected people with heads bowed, hanging their limbs in such a way that it seems they are about to fall to the ground. Some people walk on the earth in this manner to display piety. Traditions contain details about the gait of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked, he walked with vigour (not stumbling). He walked faster than all people. His gait was very beautiful and composed. Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) said: I have never seen anything more beautiful than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; it was as if the sun was moving on his blessed face. And I have never seen anyone walk faster than the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; it was as if the earth was being folded up for him. We would be anxious in every matter, but he would not be concerned. ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) said: the Messenger of Allah ﷺ walked leaning forward, so it appeared as if he was descending to a lower place. On one occasion he said that he walked as one who descends, and the gait of one who ascends was likewise like the gait of one who descends. This kind of gait is adopted by those who are determined, high-minded and brave. (Zad al-Maʿad, Ibn al-Qayyim)

Since these people are serious, dignified and upright, and since their aims are always lofty, they do not involve themselves in the foolishness and ignorance of fools, the senseless and the stupid. Therefore they do not engage in debate, argument or abuse with such people. If such an occasion arises, they extricate themselves with great grace.

﴿وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ الْجَاهِلُونَ قَالُوا سَلَامًا﴾ "And when the ignorant address them, they say, 'Peace.'" (25:63) They do this neither out of weakness, nor out of arrogance, nor because they are incapable. Rather, they keep themselves above such things. They do not spend their precious time on activities unworthy of the noble. They do so to protect themselves from obscene speech and abuse, and they devote their time to good works.

This was their conduct by day with people. As for their nights, in them they fear Allah and remain conscious of Him. They have awareness of Allah's greatness, and they fear His punishment.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah al-Furqan (25), verses 65–66**

﴿And those who say...﴾ (25:66)

The worship of Allah's servants is described here through the physical acts of prayer, prostration and standing, so that it becomes clear what their nightly activities were. When all of creation is asleep at night, they are awake. They spend their nights in prostration and standing before their Lord. They turn only to their Lord, stand with folded hands before Him alone, and prostrate only before Him. At night they give up the pleasant and sweet sleep, because they find greater delight in standing and prostrating before Allah than in that sleep. Their bodies, their souls and their thoughts are bound to Allah. Therefore, while people lie in heedless sleep, they are engaged in bowing and prostration. People lie on the earth, while they are attached to the heavens and the heights, and they are devoted to the Lord of Majesty and Bounty.

However, they do not merely assume the outward form of standing and prostration. Along with directing their thoughts to this standing, this prostration and the higher world, there is also in their hearts the fear and God-consciousness (taqwa) of Allah. This fear holds them firmly, lest they somehow be saved from the punishment of Hell. They pray at all times.

﴿Our Lord, turn away from us the punishment of Hell; indeed its punishment is ever-clinging. Indeed it is evil as a settlement and a station.﴾ (25:65–66)

They have not seen Hell with their own eyes, but they believe in its existence, and they have complete certainty in the picture that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and the Holy Quran have drawn of it. Therefore the fear that grips them, and their saying that Hell is a very terrible abode, is proof of their firm conviction and the result of their deep belief.

They turn to their Lord with utmost humility and submissiveness, so that the Generous Lord, out of His mercy, may turn away the punishment of Hell from them. They are not satisfied with worship, standing and prostration alone. They are such sensitive and God-fearing people that they do not rely upon their worship. They consider their worship to be little, and therefore they do not regard it as a complete guarantee for salvation. Along with this worship, they also seek the grace and bounty of Allah, for the punishment of Allah can be averted only through His grace and bounty.

Through the style of the discourse, Hell is depicted as a living monster. Every person is within its mouth; it calls out to every person and wants to devour every person. It stretches forth its hands and keeps taking people into its grip. Far and near are all within its reach. Out of fear of it, these servants of Allah stand before Allah day and night. Fearing it, they seek refuge in Allah, they humble themselves, and they make supplications and cries, saying: "O Allah, save us! It is devouring us!"

When they pray with their hands folded before Allah, in extreme fear and extreme anxiety, the style of the discourse creates a quivering within the atmosphere.

﴿Indeed its punishment is ever-clinging.﴾ (25:65)

That is, it is a punishment that never ends. It never leaves, does not decrease, and does not cease. This is the very quality of Hell which frightens these servants, and because of which they are always fearful and alarmed.

Then, these servants (of the Most Merciful) are a model of moderation and balance. Their lives are extremely well-balanced.

"And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor niggardly, but keep to a just balance between those" (25:67)

This is a fundamental characteristic of Islam, which it brings into being as a reality in the life of the individual Muslim and of the Muslim community. Islam keeps this characteristic in view in its system of training and morality, and in its economic and legal system. Accordingly, every part of the Islamic system rests upon the foundation of balance and moderation.

Although Islam permits the individual to possess private property, it does not give a Muslim individual a free hand to spend "his own" wealth in any manner he likes. In the capitalist system of the West, the individual has complete freedom to spend his private wealth however he wishes. Likewise, among all non-Muslim peoples the principle is the same: a person may spend his private property as he pleases, and there is no restraint upon it. But a Muslim, even in spending his private wealth, is bound to remain on the just middle path between extravagance (israf) and miserliness (kanjusi). Extravagance causes the ruin of the person, his wealth and society alike, and miserliness likewise causes loss to the person, his wealth and society, in that a person does not benefit from his wealth. For if someone benefits from his wealth and spends it, then others also gain income from it, because wealth is a collective means through which the entire society benefits. Both extravagance and miserliness harm society and collective economics. If wealth is withheld, a recession (kasad bazari) arises; and if more is spent than necessary, the purchasing power of others is affected, and then moral corruption also arises from it.

Accordingly, Islam also reforms this aspect of society, makes moderation and balance a part of the Muslim personality, and links it with faith.

"And they are, between that, moderate" (25:68) — "Rather, their spending remains balanced between the two extremes."

......

"And they are, between that, moderate" (25:68) — "Rather, their spending remains established on the balance between the two extremes."

Furthermore, a great characteristic of the servants of the Most Merciful is that they do not associate partners with Allah, do not kill any living soul, and do not commit adultery (zina). Shirk, murder and adultery are among the greatest sins (akbar al-kaba'ir) and crimes in Islam. Whoever commits these sins will certainly become liable to punishment.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verse 68:

وَالَّذِينَ ……إِلَى اللَّهِ مَتَاباً (71)

Believing in God as One, without any partner, is the foundation of the Islamic way of life. The doctrine of Tawhid (Divine Unity) is an extremely clear, straightforward and simple belief. By contrast, all other beliefs are complicated, crooked and incomprehensible. Just as a sound system of life is established upon the Islamic outlook on life, so no upright and righteous system of life can be established upon other beliefs.

Not killing any living being unjustly, and keeping the collective life of society peaceful, tranquil and secure, is the distinguishing mark of Islamic and human life. Whereas murder, plunder and looting are the characteristics of jungle life. A society in which killing and bloodshed run rampant everywhere and robbery is widespread cannot be called a human society, nor can any developmental work take place in such a society. For this reason Islam declares the killing of a soul to be a very great crime.

Likewise, Islam declares adultery to be a shameful crime, and it is only by declaring it a crime that two kinds of lives can be separated from each other. One is the kind of life in which a person raises himself a little above the filthy sexual desire of an animal and believes that the sexual union has been set for him as a lofty and exalted purpose. It is not the mere pursuit of pleasure and the filthy animal life of union between a male and a female, in which only bodily demands are fulfilled.

In short, these three qualities are the ones which create the boundary and distinction between a human and noble life and an ordinary animal and base, savage life. This is why Allah has included these three qualities among the attributes and marks of the servants of the Most Merciful (Ibad al-Rahman). Because the servants of the Most Merciful are an exalted creation in the sight of Allah, and they hold a most lofty station in His sight. This is why, after these qualities, the following warning comes:

﴿وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَلِكَ يَلْقَ أَثَاماً﴾ (25:68) "Whoever does this will receive the recompense for his sins."

The meaning of athaam here is punishment. The explanation of this punishment is then given as follows.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verse 69:

"Their punishment will be doubled on the Day of Resurrection, and they will abide therein in humiliation." (25:69) That is, not only will their punishment be doubled, but it will also be humiliating, and in this way the punishment becomes more severe and more painful.

Yes, it is not the case that whoever committed these sins even once has no way of forgiveness. He can escape this punishment through repentance (tawbah) and righteous deeds (amal salih).

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verse 70:

Except for one who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds (25:80): that is, one who, after those sins, has repented, come to faith, and begun to do righteous deeds. For such people the promise is that Allah will replace the evil deeds they committed before faith, repentance, and righteous action with good deeds.

Then Allah will change the evil deeds of such people into good deeds (25:80): this is the overflowing mercy of Allah, and a pure bounty of His generosity, for which man has no claim of entitlement. It is simply a reward for the person who abandons the wrong path, takes the path of guidance, comes under the protection of Allah, and gives up misconduct and rebellion.

And Allah is ever Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful (25:80): the door of repentance stands open at all times. Whenever a person's conscience awakens, and from whatever station one wishes to return, one can come back. Islam does not block his way, and the door of Islam is open to him. Whoever he is, however great a sinner he may be, "even if you have broken your repentance a hundred times, return."

Tabarani narrated from Abu al-Mughira, Safwan ibn Amr, Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abu Fardah: this companion came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, a man committed all sins. He left no minor sin and no major sin undone. Is there repentance for him too?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Have you embraced faith?" He said: "Yes, I have embraced Islam." The Prophet ﷺ said: "Keep doing good deeds and keep abandoning evil deeds. Allah will make even those evil deeds good for you." He said again: "And my immorality and debauchery as well?" The Prophet ﷺ said: "Yes." That man returned saying "Allahu Akbar, Allahu Akbar" until he disappeared from sight.

However, a principle of repentance is also established.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verse 71:

﴿But whoever repents and does righteous work - indeed, he turns to Allah with a [sincere] turning.﴾ (25:71)

The beginning of repentance is that a sinner feels remorse, then abandons the disobedience, and after that acts upon good deeds. Then it becomes clear that this person's repentance is sound and that he is sincere. That is, having given up evil deeds, he has begun positive progress. For disobedience is in fact an activity and a driving force in life. The person who gives up those sins will, of course, have a life free of sins, but it is also necessary to fill that void in his life with positive actions. This is the particular unit of the Islamic system of training at which it becomes evident that Allah, the Almighty, is the Creator and that He is well aware of the states of the human soul. Therefore He gave the guidance that this psychological void should be filled with righteous deeds, otherwise……

……

After this parenthetical clause, the discourse turns back again to the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful (ʿIbād al-Raḥmān).

"Those who do not bear false witness" may also be taken in its immediate and technical sense: that they do not give false testimony in a court of law, because through it people's rights are lost and the crime of assisting oppression is committed. It may also refer to genuine witnessing: if falsehood and evil are being committed in a gathering, a society or any place, these people do not attend it. That is, they keep away from a society in which evil is practised. This is the more eloquent and more moving interpretation. Likewise, they protect themselves from frivolous and indecent gatherings or occasions.

﴿And when they pass by idle talk, they pass by with dignity﴾ (25:72). ﴿They pass by with dignity.﴾ They do not involve themselves in it, nor do they take part in those evils. They neither look at nor listen to them, but pass by there like a noble and honourable person. This is because there is no empty space in the vessel of a believer's life in which frivolity and indecency could take root. When is he free from his faith, from the call of Islam and its demands? He is always busy in reforming himself and society.

……

Another attribute of the ʿIbād al-Raḥmān is that when they are reminded and admonished, they accept the lesson and advice. They believe in it; their hearts are inclined to accept the truth. They possess an alert mind and are owners of a turning, penitent heart.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 25, verse 73:

والذین ……وعمیاناً (73)

This verse contains a subtle taunt against the polytheists of Makkah: they were blindly and deafly engaged in worshipping their idols, clinging to foolish and false beliefs. They neither wished to hear any sensible word, nor did they look at clear realities with their own eyes. They neither saw the open light, nor did they walk on the straight path while seeing it. To walk face-down, blind and deaf, means to walk without thought and without reflection and understanding. This idiom paints a picture of a state that reveals the extreme of heedlessness and foolishness, in which there is no reflection at all. As for the servants of Allah and the servants of the Most Merciful, they settle every matter with the utmost thought and understanding. They look to see where the truth lies in these beliefs. They find that such and such proofs and evidences establish the truth. Their faith is ʿalā wajh al-baṣīrah (based on insight), so they do not fall face-down on any matter like the ignorant. Their faith is ʿalā wajh al-baṣīrah, so they do not fall face-down on any matter like the ignorant. If there is zeal and fervour found in them regarding their beliefs, then it is found ʿalā wajh al-baṣīrah; it is not found ʿalā wajh al-jahālah (in ignorance). They are ʿārif, possessors of insight.

At last, they do not confine themselves merely to prostration and standing (in prayer) before the Lord, nor to gathering these other great qualities within themselves. Rather, they also hope for offspring after them who will walk in their way. Their wives too should be like them. Seeing them, their eyes should be cooled. Their hearts should be content concerning them. And in this way, through their wives and children, the number of the servants of the Most Merciful should increase. And they also hope that they may be a good example for the righteous servants of God even in distant places.

﴿And those who say: "Our Lord, grant us from our wives and offspring the delight of our eyes, and make us a leader (imam) for the God-fearing."﴾ (25:74)

This is a profound natural and faith-based consciousness: every sincere believer desires that his companions be many, that all people turn toward God, and before others, a person thinks about his wives and children, that they should come into line with him. For it is most of all one's own offspring who can be inclined to obey him, and it is most of all one who is answerable regarding his children and family. Then, too, it is a natural desire in every believer, and it ought to be, that he be an example and leader of goodness. Those who turn to God should take a lesson from his life. The wish to be an example for the believers and the foremost among the believers is not a sign of pride or the impulse of superiority, but the impulse of advancing ahead in goodness; otherwise all believers are travelers on one and the same path.

……

Now it is also explained here what will be the end and reward of such servants of the Most Merciful.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 75–76:

أُولَٰئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ ... وَمَقَامًا (76)

The word "ghurfah" (غرفہ) means a lofty dwelling, which refers to Paradise. Alternatively, it may refer to a particular station within Paradise, just as an upper room is more desirable than an ordinary house on the ground. Every person seats Muslims in upper rooms, and since these people are also honoured and esteemed servants of Allah, and since the title "ʿIbād al-Raḥmān" (the servants of the Most Merciful) is used for them and their qualities have been enumerated, they will be received in this special station with greeting, blessing and peace. This is because they were patient in the world and remained steadfast upon these qualities. From this it is known that following these qualities and signs of the ʿIbād al-Raḥmān is no easy matter. Great patience and perseverance are required. On the path of life, deceptive desires keep away from every side. Places to fall and slip are present everywhere along this path. To walk straight along this long highway of life, determination and perseverance are needed. For this reason Allah mentions here "bi-mā ṣabarū" (25:85).

And in contrast to that Hell, from which they constantly pray to be saved, and which is a very evil place, there will be a place for them. That is Paradise, which is an excellent place, and where they will remain forever.

﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾ (25:89) "They will abide therein forever; how excellent it is as a place of rest and a station." Here they will have no need to leave, and they will remain there in complete peace and tranquility.

……

The portrait of the ʿIbād al-Raḥmān has already been drawn, and the details of the qualities of the essence and cream of humanity have been given. Now these people are being given this honour: that if these servants of Allah were not there, then in the sight of Allah the entire humanity would not even have the weight of a worthless thing. As for the deniers, a final decision of the punishment of Hell has already been made for them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verses 75–76:

أُولَٰئِكَ يُجْزَوْنَ ... وَمَقَامًا (76)

The word "ghurfah" (غرفہ) means a lofty dwelling, which refers to Paradise. Alternatively, it may refer to a particular station within Paradise, just as an upper room is more desirable than an ordinary house on the ground. Every person seats Muslims in upper rooms, and since these people are also honoured and esteemed servants of Allah, and since the title "ʿIbād al-Raḥmān" (the servants of the Most Merciful) is used for them and their qualities have been enumerated, they will be received in this special station with greeting, blessing and peace. This is because they were patient in the world and remained steadfast upon these qualities. From this it is known that following these qualities and signs of the ʿIbād al-Raḥmān is no easy matter. Great patience and perseverance are required. On the path of life, deceptive desires keep away from every side. Places to fall and slip are present everywhere along this path. To walk straight along this long highway of life, determination and perseverance are needed. For this reason Allah mentions here "bi-mā ṣabarū" (25:85).

And in contrast to that Hell, from which they constantly pray to be saved, and which is a very evil place, there will be a place for them. That is Paradise, which is an excellent place, and where they will remain forever.

﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا ۚ حَسُنَتْ مُسْتَقَرًّا وَمُقَامًا﴾ (25:89) "They will abide therein forever; how excellent it is as a place of rest and a station." Here they will have no need to leave, and they will remain there in complete peace and tranquility.

……

The portrait of the ʿIbād al-Raḥmān has already been drawn, and the details of the qualities of the essence and cream of humanity have been given. Now these people are being given this honour: that if these servants of Allah were not there, then in the sight of Allah the entire humanity would not even have the weight of a worthless thing. As for the deniers, a final decision of the punishment of Hell has already been made for them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 25, verse 77:

Qul ma ya'budu bikum... lizaman (77) (al-Rub')

This is a concluding statement which is in harmony with the whole surah. The central theme of this entire surah is to console the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The purpose of this surah is to remove the burden upon the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ) caused by the people's denial and their turning away, because those people, while knowing the station of Muhammad (ﷺ), had insisted on denial and displayed obstinacy, which was the more painful matter. Therefore it is explained here what the status of these people is. The whole of humanity is not equal to a grain of dust in the sight of Allah. Respect and regard for humanity with Allah is due only to those of His servants whose qualities have been enumerated, who constantly call upon Allah and humble themselves.

What is the status of these people? What is the status of the whole human population? And then what is the status of this entire earth? In the universe of Allah, it is but a particle, and humanity is like any living creature (for example, a mosquito) in this world. Of the nations of this earth, one nation... what then are its past generations and all the coming generations? Indeed, the Book of Allah is the universe's few pages, and the remaining pages of this universal book—knowledge of them belongs to Allah alone.

And man, despite this worthlessness and this lack of value, puffs himself up and continues to puff himself up, and considers himself a great thing. Then he becomes rebellious. Then so rebellious that he begins to show disrespect in the presence of his Creator. Whereas he is not even a thing; in comparison with Allah he is weaker and more deficient. Indeed, the source of his strength is only Allah. By being joined to Allah, man can become something and can be counted. He can also find the path of guidance. If he finds the path of guidance and is joined to Allah, then his weight in the scale of Allah becomes significant. Indeed, in the scales of Allah he can become heavier even than the angels. Because the disposition that Allah gave to man, and the command He gave to the angels to prostrate before him, was so that man would recognize Allah, attain access to Him, and become His servant. Only in this way can he preserve those distinctive qualities, attributes and marks, on account of which he was given preference over the angels, and on account of which the angels prostrated before him; otherwise he is nothing at all. Without this, if the whole of humanity were placed in the scale of Allah, it would not equal even a mosquito. In the scale and balance of Allah, this earth is but a particle.

Qul ma ya'budu bikum rabbi lawla du'a'ukum (25:77): "Say to the people: What concern would my Lord have with you, were it not for your calling upon Him?" This manner of speech is a great support for the Prophet (ﷺ). It is said: O people, if you do not believe, then what is your standing, and if you are not counted among the servants of Allah, then you are nothing. You will become fuel for Hell.

Faqad kadhdhabtum fasawfa yakunu lizaman (25:77): "Now that you have denied, soon there will be a punishment from which escape will be impossible."
